10 countries where getting citizenship is difficult for Nigerians, others
items.description: For millions of people around the world, obtaining citizenship in a second country can provide greater security, mobility and long-term opportunities. While many countries have established routes for foreign residents to become citizens, others impose lengthy residency periods, strict language and integration requirements, limited eligibility or highly discretionary approval processes. In some cases, simply meeting the legal requirements does not guarantee success. Authorities may retain broad powers over who can ultimately be granted citizenship, while countries such as Japan and China also place restrictions on dual nationality. Here are 10 countries where obtaining citizenship can be particularly difficult for foreigners. Qatar Qatar has one of the world’s most restrictive naturalisation systems. Foreign applicants generally need to have lived in the country for 25 years before becoming eligible, alongside requirements including Arabic proficiency and good conduct. Even after meeting the conditions, citizenship is not guaranteed, with approvals tightly controlled by the authorities. Vatican City Vatican City does not operate a conventional citizenship-by-residency system. Citizenship is generally connected to specific positions or official responsibilities within the Holy See. It can therefore end when the individual’s qualifying role comes to an end, making it fundamentally different from traditional naturalisation systems. Liechtenstein Liechtenstein is known for its lengthy route to citizenship, with naturalisation potentially requiring decades of residence. Applicants can also face local and national approval procedures, making citizenship a highly selective process in the small European principality. Bhutan Bhutan maintains strict citizenship rules aimed at protecting its national identity and culture. Foreign applicants face demanding residency, cultural and integration requirements, while final approval is subject to government scrutiny. The country’s approach makes naturalisation considerably harder than simply establishing long-term residence. Saudi Arabia Saudi Arabian citizenship is generally far easier to obtain through family heritage than through naturalisation. The kingdom has opened limited opportunities for certain highly skilled professionals and individuals with exceptional expertise. However, applicants still face demanding requirements and decisions remain heavily dependent on government approval. Kuwait Kuwait maintains tight controls over who can become a citizen. Naturalisation is restricted to specific categories and can involve lengthy residency and other eligibility requirements. The country’s restrictive nationality framework has also contributed to longstanding debates surrounding its sizeable stateless population. Switzerland Switzerland has a demanding naturalisation system that combines federal requirements with assessments at cantonal and municipal levels. Foreign residents generally need around 10 years of residence, as well as evidence of language ability and successful integration. Local authorities can play an important part in deciding whether an applicant qualifies. China China rarely grants citizenship to foreign nationals and does not generally recognise dual citizenship. Foreigners seeking naturalisation typically need Chinese family connections or another legally recognised basis for their application. Because approvals are uncommon and the criteria are narrowly applied, acquiring Chinese citizenship can be extremely difficult. North Korea North Korea has no widely accessible or transparent naturalisation route comparable with those found in many other countries. Citizenship is predominantly determined by birth and state classification, leaving foreign nationals with very limited opportunities to obtain citizenship through ordinary residency. Japan Japan has a formal naturalisation process, but applicants must satisfy a range of conditions. Foreign residents generally need at least five years of continuous residence, financial stability and evidence of good conduct. Japan also generally requires applicants to give up their existing nationality when naturalising, making the process particularly demanding for people seeking to retain dual citizenship. items.title: Camp Vacances Faso Mêbo 2026 : Le calendrier et les lieux dévoilés
items.description: L’Agence Faso Mêbo a dévoilé, le samedi 8 août, le programme officiel de l’édition 2026 du Camp Vacances Faso Mêbo. La manifestation se tiendra du 10 au 24 août dans les six régions militaires du Burkina Faso. Dans un communiqué publié sur ses plateformes numériques, l’agence informe les candidats et leurs parents que les listes des participants retenus sont désormais consultables sur son site web officiel ainsi que sur sa page Facebook. La sélection a été effectuée à l’issue d’un processus rigoureux, combinant inscriptions en ligne, examen des dossiers et tirage au sort digital. Pour cette édition, les activités se déploieront selon le calendrier régional suivant. Dans la région de Kadiogo, à Ouagadougou, elles se dérouleront du lundi 10 au mercredi 19 août. À Koulsé (Kaya) et à Bankui (Dédougou), elles auront lieu du mardi 11 au jeudi 20 août. Dans les régions de Liptako (Dori) et de Goulmou (Fada), le camp est prévu du jeudi 13 au samedi 22 août. Enfin, à Guiriko (Bobo-Dioulasso), il se tiendra du samedi 15 au lundi 24 août. L’Agence Faso Mêbo invite les jeunes sélectionnés et leurs familles à prendre toutes les dispositions utiles pour respecter ce calendrier. Placé sous le signe de l’engagement citoyen et de la contribution à l’édification nationale, ce camp vise à renforcer le lien entre jeunesse et construction collective. items.title: Police form new team to probe Mir Raza Ali's murder; murder charge added to FIR
items.description: KARACHI: The investigation team probing the killing of 25-year-old businessman Mir Raza Ali has been reconstituted while the murder charge has been added to the case registered on his father’s complaint. Ali’s body was found in bushes in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar last month, a day after he went missing on July 28. While his family is convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police had previously been building the case around the possibility that he died by suicide. However, an order released by the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office on Sunday, notifying the reconstitution of the investigating team, showed that the murder charge had been added to the first information report. The order, seen by Dawn , said the new investigating team was formed in light of Ali’s second postmortem report, which contradicted the one released after his first postmortem, to “supervise the investigation of FIR no. 795/2026 u/s 365/ 302/ 201 of the PPC”. Initially, the first information report (FIR) was registered only under Section 365 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), which pertains to kidnapping. Of the newly added sections, 302 pertains to murder and 201 to hiding the evidence of an offence or giving false information to screen the offender. The case would now be probed by a five-member team led by Sindh Deputy IG (Crime and Investigation) Amir Farooqui and comprising Alfalah SSP Syed Muhammad Ali Raza, Korangi SP (Investigation) Qais Khan, Central SP (Investigation) Anam Tajjamul and Zaman Town SIO Ch. Ghazanfar, the police order said. It added: “The team shall undertake a comprehensive and impartial investigation into the case from all relevant angles. The team shall identify, collect, preserve and examine any new or additional evidence and shall thoroughly examine and analyse all physical, technical, circumstantial and forensic evidence collected during the investigation. “The team shall make all out efforts to work out the case and submit a report to the court concerned within the stipulated period. The team may co-opt any officer to assist in the investigation. Progress shall be reported on a day-to-day basis.” On Saturday, the lawyer for Ali’s family, Jibran Nasir, had demanded that the first investigation probing the case be replaced, after a fresh post-mortem examination conducted following the exhumation of Ali’s body found that he had been shot in the back — evidence that ruled out the possibility of suicide. Speaking to the media, he reiterated the allegation that Ali had been tortured before being murdered. “This was murder following torture — the murder of a happy, ambitious and educated young man from Karachi,” he alleged. The family’s lawyer also criticised senior police officials, alleging that they “do not want to investigate, but rather humiliate, harass and exhaust the family”. Advocate Nasir added that he and the family had “no faith” in the investigation team and that they wanted the entire team changed. Controversy over autopsy Raza, an Institute of Business Administration graduate and the owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. The latest developments in his case follow a controversy between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding Ali’s first post-mortem examination. Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel on Tuesday that the postmortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs. The police surgeon, whose assessment was based only on the post-mortem report and photographs as she had not examined the body herself back then, had said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another. The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case. Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation. The statement, however, said that exhumation of the dead body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission. On Thursday, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Raza’s father, Mir Hussain Ali, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation. The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Dr Syed as the convener. Prof Dr Naseem Ahmed of Dow University of Health Sciences, Dr Farah Waseem of Jinnah Sindh Medical University, Amir Hassan Khan of Citizens Police Liaison Committee, Additional Police Surgeon Dr Sirichand, Dr Kamran Khan and Dr Daniyal Mirza of Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre, and Dr Mohammed Yaseen, the admin in-charge of the police surgeon office, were the other members of the board. However, in the early hours of Friday, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department. While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed to Prof Dr Zakiuddin from DUHS, Prof Dr Kazi Akbar and Prof Dr Abid Hussain Chang from Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, and Hyderabad Police Surgeon Dr Waseem Khan. On Friday morning, Raza’s family was present at the Tariq Road graveyard for the exhumation, which was deferred after they objected ti the new board. Standing alongside Raza’s father, Nasir had accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts and held the police, health department and the Sindh government responsible for the delay. The Sindh government then restored the original medical board on Friday, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on Saturday. After a second postmortem of the body, Dr Syed told Dawn, “We have collected samples for identification, chemical analysis and gunshot residue. The cause of death is reserved for laboratory reports.” Regarding the autopsy, she said that multiple injuries were found on the head and face. “Fractured rib on the back, which is the entry wound of the gunshot [that] exited from the front,” she said. She said the body bore “injuries in right flank and feet [and] congealed black substance present in mouth and throat”.

items.title: «Enfant gâté» de l’Occident : la diplomatie russe fustige la transformation de l'Ukraine en un «véritable État voyou à qui tout est permis»
items.description: Dans l'interet d'une serie d'acteurs geopolitiques, l'Ukraine « est soudainement devenue un veritable etat voyou », capable de faire tout ce qu'il veut sans en subir les consequences, a declare Rodion Mirochnik, ambassadeur charge de missions speciales au ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, dans une interview accordee a l'agence TASS. Selon lui, Kiev estime qu'il peut tout se permettre. « a quoi bon traiter avec lui ? Il peut s'en prendre aux entreprises kazakhes, affectant ainsi l'economie exterieure de l'etat kazakh, et il s'en tirera sans aucune consequence. S'il s'en prend a la flotte de plusieurs autres etats, la encore, il s'en tirera egalement sans aucune consequence. C'est donc une sorte d'enfant gâte, eleve par la societe occidentale, qui est completement fou, a qui il ne faut pas avoir affaire, d'autant plus qu'on ne lui fera rien », a souligne Rodion Mirochnik. D'apres lui, l'Ukraine est tout simplement a la charge de l'Occident qui doit donc « gerer cette charge : la direction dans laquelle l'Ukraine doit aller, les cibles qu'elle doit viser et la maniere de l'utiliser ». « Il s'agit donc ici d'une sorte d'experience a l'echelle mondiale, qui a permis de creer un etat docile, un etat kamikaze, mercenaire. On pourrait citer de tres nombreux synonymes. Ce n'est meme pas une experience mais une pratique geopolitique, grâce a laquelle des pays, qui veulent faire croire que ce n'est pas eux qui sont impliques, continuent neanmoins d'utiliser cet etat, tout un peuple, des territoires entiers, des economies et des secteurs a leur avantage : c'est-a-dire de l'utiliser pour poursuivre leur propre politique », a conclu l'ambassadeur charge de missions speciales du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres. Fin juillet, l'administration presidentielle americaine a averti l'Ukraine que les attaques contre des navires en mer Noire n'ayant aucun lien avec la Russie etaient inacceptables. Cette reaction faisait suite a une intervention de Mike Wirth, PDG de la societe energetique americaine Chevron, concernant les frappes contre des petroliers et le terminal du Caspian Pipeline Consortium a Novorossiisk, sur la cote de la mer Noire, dont Chevron detient 15 % des parts. Le 7 août, Bloomberg a rapporte que l'Ukraine s'etait engagee a ne pas frapper les infrastructures du Consortium, ni certains navires se dirigeant vers son terminal en mer Noire. Avant les negociations entre Washington et Kiev, plusieurs incidents se sont produits dans la zone du terminal. Le 30 juillet, deux petroliers se trouvant a proximite des installations du Consortium ont ete pris pour cible. Aucun deces ni deversement de carburant n'a ete signale. Le Consortium a toutefois souligne que ces attaques se produisaient malgre les appels du Kazakhstan et d'autres actionnaires etrangers a ne pas porter atteinte a cette infrastructure energetique internationale. Moscou, pour sa part, a fermement condamne ces attaques contre les installations du Consortium. Le 30 juillet, la porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, Maria Zakharova, les a qualifiees de « terrorisme » et a condamne ces frappes comme etant dirigees contre des infrastructures energetiques civiles.

items.title: P-Square destroyed the biggest brand Africa produced – Daddy Showkey
items.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Veteran Nigerian singer Daddy Showkey has expressed disappointment over the prolonged rift between twin brothers Peter and Paul Okoye of P-Square, saying the duo destroyed what he described as the biggest music brand Africa ever produced. Speaking during an interview with Goldmyne TV, Daddy Showkey said, “P-Square destroyed the biggest brand that Africa produced. P-Square isn’t for them alone.” The music veteran stressed that entertainers owe their success to the public, noting that fans should always be considered in major decisions. Drawing from his personal experience, he said, “As an entertainer I can decide to lock myself in my room and celebrate my 50 years on stage. I am celebrating because it is the people that made me Daddy Showkey. If the people have made you, you are not considering them but considering how much you guys are making.” He warned that the consequences of the brothers’ ongoing feud would become clearer with time, adding that their relationship should take precedence over their differences. “Dragging themselves like this, the future will tell. No matter what, you guys are brothers. No matter what, you should look for a place to resolve things because you have children. Tomorrow you will carry this beef to your children,” he said. Daddy Showkey’s comments come amid the lingering public dispute involving Peter, Paul, and their elder brother Jude, who previously managed the music duo, following disagreements that have continued to attract public attention. items.title: Les lettres latines intègrent les plaques d'immatriculation au Maroc
items.description: La publication au Bulletin Officiel n° 7531, en date du 3 août 2026, de l'arrêté n° 640.26 du ministre du Transport et de la Logistique, signé le 26 mars 2026, acte le changement du cadre réglementaire du système d'immatriculation automobile relatif aux véhicules à moteur et aux remorques. Il est désormais obligatoire d'intégrer des lettres latines aux côtés des lettres arabes sur les plaques d'immatriculation. Ainsi, la deuxième partie du numéro d'immatriculation, communément appelée la série, devra se composer d'une ou deux lettres en langue arabe tracées en calligraphie marocaine unifiée, associées à leur équivalent en caractères latins. Cette réforme vise à standardiser l'identification des véhicules et à simplifier leur lecture, notamment lors des déplacements transfrontaliers. Le changement de plaque ne sera pas immédiatement obligatoire pour l'ensemble des automobilistes. Pour les véhicules circulant sur le territoire national, les propriétaires peuvent conserver leurs plaques actuelles jusqu'à la première mutation de propriété, moment auquel le nouveau modèle bilingue sera attribué lors de la cession du véhicule. Concernant les véhicules immatriculés au Maroc circulant à l'étranger, l'utilisation des plaques actuelles reste autorisée jusqu'au 31 décembre 2026, apportant ainsi une clarification réglementaire aux contrôles routiers subis en Europe, notamment en Espagne et en Italie. Pour les deux-roues, tricycles et quadricycles légers, les dispositions relatives à la nouvelle immatriculation entreront en vigueur à partir du 1er janvier 2027, leurs titres de propriété et plaques actuels restant valides jusqu'au transfert de propriété ou à la demande d'un duplicata. Enfin, le texte réglementaire introduit une simplification administrative pour les achats effectués via le financement participatif Murabaha, en autorisant le vendeur concessionnaire à déposer directement le dossier de demande du certificat d'immatriculation et du titre de propriété pour le compte de l'acquéreur. The post Les lettres latines intègrent les plaques d'immatriculation au Maroc appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: New autopsy finds Mir Ali Raza was shot in the back, suffered multiple injuries
items.description: • Eight-member board exhumed the corpse in presence of magistrate, family • Police surgeon says cause of death reserved till receipt of reports • Says young businessman suffered injuries on head and face • Family lawyer wants investigation team replaced KARACHI: A fresh post-mortem examination conducted following the exhumation of the body of young business owner Mir Ali Raza on Saturday found that he had been shot in the back, evidence that ruled out the possibility of suicide. Sources told Dawn that an eight-member medical board that exhumed the body in the presence of a judicial magistrate at the Tariq Road graveyard also found “multiple injuries on the head and face” and “fractures on the nasal bone and skull” that indicated he might have been subjected to torture before being fatally shot. Raza, owner of eatery Wafflix, had gone missing on July 28. The 25-year-old’s body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar. While his family is convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, investigators probing the incident said they found evidence that strengthened the possibility that he died by suicide. A controversy over flawed autopsy report and investigations compelled Raza’s family to file an application before a judicial magistrate for exhumation of the body for a fresh post-mortem examination. On Saturday, the eight-member board, headed by Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed, in the presence of a magistrate, victim’s family and lawyer and the investigating officer of the case performed the exhumation. The post-mortem examination continued for one hour and fifteen minutes and the body was buried again at around 1:33pm “We have collected samples for positive identification, chemical analysis and gunshot residue. The cause of death is kept reserved for laboratory reports,” Dr Syed told Dawn . Regarding autopsy, she said that multiple injuries were found on the head and face. “Fractured rib on the back which is the entry wound of the gunshot [that] exit from front,” she said. She said the body bore “injuries in right flank and feet [and] congealed black substance present in mouth and throat”. Lawyer demands new investigation team Later in the evening, lawyer for Raza’s family Advocate Jibran Nasir alleged that the 25-year-old had been tortured before being murdered and demanded that the entire investigation team be replaced. Speaking to the media, he said the medical report of the second post-mortem detailed some of the alleged injuries Raza had sustained before his death. “This was murder following torture — the murder of a happy, ambitious and educated young man from Karachi,” he alleged. The lawyer said that Raza had wounds to his forehead and a fractured nose, as well as swelling and congealed blood around his lower jaw, consistent with having been punched. “There is a fracture to his temple above his ear, indicating he was struck,” he alleged. “In the tongue area, a congealed black substance was discovered, which is not naturally found in the body. This substance has been taken and sent to a lab to see what he was forced to ingest,” he said. “Now we come to the firearm injury, where it was earlier said that he was shot in the chest and the bullet exited through his back. We have now proven 110 per cent that the bullet entered his back and exited after breaking and fracturing his ribs,” he said, referring to the fresh autopsy. The family’s lawyer also criticised senior police officials, alleging that they “do not want to investigate, but rather humiliate, harass and exhaust the family”. “They are finding months-old recordings and frustrating, emotionally exhausting and humiliating Mir Hussain and Maryam Hussain. Are you investigating or harassing them? They sat them in their offices and told them repeatedly, ‘It’s a suicide, accept it’,” the advocate claimed further. Advocate Nasir added that he and the family had “no faith” in the investigation team and that they wanted the entire team changed. Raza’s father, Mir Hussain, told reporters that he had maintained since July 30 that his son’s death was a brutal murder. “We saw the body and told them [that it was murder], but they kept saying, ‘Suicide, suicide, suicide,’” he said. Mir Hussain said it “brought us peace” to learn that their claims that Raza had been attacked before his death were true. “We have said it was murder from the start,” he added. “Why are they hiding the killers?” Published in Dawn, August 9th, 2026

items.title: Publish your assets, reject vote-buying, SERAP to Tinubu, Atiku, Obi, 16 others
items.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has urged “all 19 presidential candidates announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to promptly publish details of their assets and liabilities, those of their spouses and, where applicable, their unmarried children under 18, and disclose the legitimate sources of their significant assets ahead of the 2027 presidential election.” SERAP, in a statement on Sunday signed by its deputy director, Kolawole Oluwadare, also called on “all presidential candidates to publicly and unequivocally reject vote-buying and electoral bribery before and during the elections, and to instruct their parties, campaign organisations, agents and supporters not to offer or distribute money, gifts or other material inducements in exchange for votes.” The presidential candidates are President Bola Tinubu (APC), Atiku Abubakar (ADC), Peter Obi (NDC), Senator Sandy Onor (PDP), Omoyele Sowore (AAC), Donald Duke (PRP), Okwori Ada Elizabeth Frederick (NDP), Chukwu Anita Zugwai (YPP), Rufai Adekunle Omoaje (AA), and Adenuga Sunday (Boot Party). Others are Memeh Samuel (DLA), Nwanyanwu Daniel Danerechukwu (ZLP), Okereke Sunday Chibuzor (LP), Okereke Iken Esther (NRM), Abbas-Bin Aliyu (ADP), Dikwa Suleiman Mohammed (NNPP), Adebayo Adewole Ebenezer (SDP), Seyi Makinde (APM), and Yusuf Kabiru (APP). In an open letter to the candidates dated 8 August 2026 and signed by SERAP Deputy Director Kolawole Oluwadare, the organisation urged “the candidates to go beyond the bare legal minimum and voluntarily embrace higher standards of transparency, accountability and integrity in seeking Nigeria’s highest elected office.” SERAP said: “Candidates asking Nigerians to entrust them with enormous constitutional powers over public finances, natural resources, appointments and security institutions should be willing, before asking for their votes, to demonstrate that their personal financial affairs can withstand reasonable public scrutiny.” According to SERAP: “Nigeria’s democracy belongs to its citizens. Votes must not be bought. Public office must not be treated as private property. Those seeking the highest public office must be willing to meet the highest standards of transparency, accountability and integrity.” The letter, read in part: “Nigerians should not be asked to choose between candidates on the basis of who can spend the most money. They should be able to choose on the basis of policies, competence, integrity, character and their vision for Nigeria.” “Voluntary pre-election disclosure would enable voters to assess potential conflicts of interest and significant sources of wealth, strengthen public confidence in the electoral process, and establish a baseline against which future changes in assets could be assessed if a candidate is elected.” “The 2027 presidential election presents an opportunity for political leaders to show that public office is a public trust. Candidates who voluntarily disclose their assets and reject vote-buying can show that they are prepared to uphold the transparency and accountability they promise to deliver if elected.” “The Nigerian Constitution 1999 (as amended) and international human rights standards protect free and informed electoral choice, making transparency essential to meaningful democratic participation and providing a strong basis for candidates seeking the highest public office to voluntarily disclose relevant financial information, particularly where corruption and vote-buying threaten electoral integrity.” “Although the Nigerian Constitution does not expressly require presidential candidates to publish their asset declarations before an election, the Constitution, read as a whole, embodies principles of transparency, accountability, integrity in public office and meaningful participation in government.” “The Constitution already requires elected public officers, including the President, to declare their assets and liabilities.” “Paragraph 11 of Part I of the Fifth Schedule requires public officers to submit declarations of their properties, assets and liabilities, including those of unmarried children under 18, while section 140(1) requires a person elected President to make the prescribed declaration before assuming the functions of office.” “Article 25 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights protects citizens’ rights to participate in public affairs and to vote and be elected in genuine periodic elections. These rights cannot be meaningfully exercised where voters are denied relevant information necessary to scrutinise those seeking to govern them.” “We are also concerned about the persistent use of money, gifts and other inducements to influence voters. Vote-buying directly undermines the constitutional principle that sovereignty belongs to the people.” “Section 14(2)(a) of the Constitution provides that sovereignty belongs to the people of Nigeria, from whom government derives its powers and authority, while section 125 of the Electoral Act 2026 criminalises bribery and related conduct intended to procure the return of a person to elective office or the vote of an elector.” “An election in which citizens’ votes are purchased, coerced or otherwise financially induced cannot genuinely reflect the free political will of the Nigerian people.” “Vote-buying is particularly harmful in circumstances of poverty and economic hardship because it exploits economic vulnerability and risks transforming a constitutional political right into a financial transaction.” “Candidates seeking the presidency have a particular responsibility to demonstrate that they are prepared to uphold the standards of transparency, accountability and integrity expected of public office holders.” “The choice before Nigerians in 2027 should be a choice based on ideas, policies, competence and integrity—not on who can spend the most money or conceal the most wealth.” SERAP therefore urged all 19 presidential candidates to urgently: Publish their assets and liabilities before the election, including relevant assets and liabilities of their spouses and unmarried children under 18; Disclose the legitimate sources of significant assets, including business interests, investments, real property, substantial gifts and inheritance, while protecting legitimate personal security and privacy; Commit to updating their public declarations if elected and explaining material increases in wealth; Publicly reject vote-buying and electoral bribery, including conduct undertaken through campaign organisations, agents, supporters or political associates; Instruct their campaign organisations and political associates not to distribute money, gifts, food, transportation benefits or other material inducements in exchange for votes; Report credible allegations of vote-buying involving their campaign organisations to the appropriate authorities; and Sign and publish a public integrity pledge committing themselves, their parties and campaign organisations to peaceful, transparent, accountable and corruption-free elections The post Publish your assets, reject vote-buying, SERAP to Tinubu, Atiku, Obi, 16 others appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Five dead in new Russia, Ukraine strikes
items.description: Russian strikes killed two people and wounded dozens across Ukraine overnight Saturday and Sunday, while a Ukrainian drone attack killed three people in Russia’s Belgorod region. More than four years after the start of Russia’s large-scale offensive against Ukraine, the two warring countries are ramping up long-range strikes, causing a growing number of civilian casualties. Russia is relying on “ballistic terror,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on social media, stating that 61 missiles of various types had been fired at his country this week. “More pressure, more sanctions against Russia and more air defence for Ukraine are needed,” he said. The two people killed by a Russian drone strike were in the major northeastern city of Kharkiv, where four floors of a residential building were also destroyed, Zelensky. Twenty-three people were also injured, according to regional governor Oleg Synegoubov. Images he shared show a gutted building with emergency services working at the scene. According to the Ukrainian president, eight people were also injured overnight in Odesa, where strikes damaged the power grid, the port, and residential buildings. Zelensky condemned another “absolutely brutal” strike targeting energy infrastructure near a shopping centre in Pavlohrad, in the Dnipropetrovsk region. Nine people, including four children, were injured there, he said. Images posted on social media Saturday evening — which AFP has not been able to verify — show buildings on fire in what appears to be a commercial area. In Russia, a Ukrainian drone attack on the border city of Belgorod killed three people, according to the region’s acting governor, Alexander Shuvaev. Twenty-five people, including children aged four and nine, were also injured, he added. Fires broke out in cars, two apartment buildings, and a house, according to him. A video released by Russian media shows an apartment building engulfed in flames at night, watched by residents gathered across the street. According to the United Nations, the conflict has claimed more civilian lives this year. The Russian invasion, which began four and a half years ago, continues with prospects of a peace agreement largely stalled. bur-led/st/cw The post Five dead in new Russia, Ukraine strikes appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Osun election: APC candidate eyes creative, sports industries to empower youths
items.description: By Shina Abubakar Osogbo The Osun State gubernatorial candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Mr. Bola Oyebamiji, AMBO, has assured that youths will be the fulcrum of his administration’s decision-making if elected governor. He added that his leverage the numerous opportunities available in the creative and sports industry to drive youth development and enhance inclusion in governance. Oyebamiji gave the assurance during the Osun Youths Interactive Session held at Adolak Event Centre, Osogbo, where youths from different sectors, including students, professionals, civil society organisations, artisans, community groups and other clusters, engaged him on his vision for the state. The interactive session, organised by the Directorate of Youths, Students of the APC campaign council, was designed as a platform for young people to understand the APC candidate’s PROSPERITY Agenda and engage directly on issues affecting their future. Oyebamiji expressed confidence in his electoral prospects, noting that his campaign engagements across the 30 local government areas of Osun State had provided him with direct understanding of the expectations and aspirations of the people. “We shall be duly elected come August 15th. This is because we have traversed all the 30 local government areas of the state in three different periods: the pre-primary period, the period of inaugurating the party canvassers, and finally the direct campaign interface with the people of Osun State,” he said. On youth development, he said, “sport is a critical sector capable of driving economic growth and creating opportunities for young people. We have been holding strategic consultations on sports development and envisioned a strong sports club in the Southwest where governors across the region could collaborate to promote sporting excellence”. Earlier, the Chairman of the Directorate, Mr. Ayodele Asalu (Asler), described the gathering as more than a political meeting, noting that it was designed as an open conversation between the candidate and young people across different backgrounds. Asalu said the future of Osun State required young people to be active participants in governance rather than merely being mobilised during elections. He stressed that issues such as education, employment, skills development, entrepreneurship, technology, creative economy and youth participation in government remained central to the concerns of young people. Also, the Chairman of the Planning Committee, Kehinde Ayantunji, while discussing the expectations of the interactive section, said the current administration in the state has destroyed sports infrastructure and has little or no achievement on youth development. According to him, for almost four years, the state has not had a common football pitch to play ordinary local league while the youth virtuous values have been replaced with brigandage and thuggery, which makes the youth population less productive. The Lead Discussant, Dr. Lekan Olatunji, explained that the PROSPERITY Agenda was developed with youth inclusion as a major focus, stressing that young people were involved in shaping the manifesto. Olatunji highlighted key areas of the agenda, including improved education, skills development, support for small and medium enterprises, talent development, creative economy, sports, agriculture and youth-focused wealth creation initiatives. Chairman of the occasion, Eng. Olamilekan Badmus urged the youths to vote massively for Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji in the August 15 Governorship election, assuring the youth that the future and economic prosperity of the state is secure under Oyebamiji. items.title: WAFCON 2026: Morocco to face winner of Super Falcons’ clash with Cameroon
items.description: Morocco will face either Nigeria or Cameroon in the semi-finals of the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) after securing a 2-1 victory over South Africa on Saturday night. The Atlas Lionesses advanced to the last four after overcoming the reigning African champions in a closely contested quarter-final. Sakina Ouzraoui opened the scoring for the hosts before Hanan Ait El Haj extended Morocco’s advantage from the penalty spot. South Africa, known as Banyana Banyana, pulled one back through Thembi Kgatlana in the 67th minute, but Morocco held firm to secure their place in the semi-finals. The hosts will now await the outcome of Sunday’s quarter-final between Nigeria and Cameroon to discover their next opponents. A potential meeting with Nigeria would add another chapter to the rivalry between the two sides, with Morocco having lost to the Super Falcons in the final of the previous WAFCON edition. The Super Falcons defeated Morocco in the 2024 final to claim their 10th continental title. Morocco will be aiming to go one step further on home soil this time as they pursue their first WAFCON title. The semi-final place has also guaranteed Morocco qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. All four WAFCON semi-finalists will automatically qualify for next year’s global tournament. items.title: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked Saudi Aramco Jazan refinery, fire extinguished
items.description: Aug 9 (Reuters) - Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on Sunday, two days after the kingdom signed a defence pact with Turkey and Pakistan. The Saudi energy ministry said a fire had broken out at the refinery that was later extinguished, without saying what caused the fire. It said the relevant authorities were completing procedures to deal with the incident, which processes 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day in southwestern Saudi Arabia. No injuries were reported, it added.

items.title: Security forces kill 15 terrorists in Balochistan IBOs: state media
items.description: Security forces have killed 15 terrorists in multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in several areas of Balochistan, state media reported on Sunday. State-run Pakistan TV reported citing sources that the IBOs were carried out in Mastung, Bolan, Washuk, Awaran, Sibi, Khuzdar, Harnai, and Nushki under Operation Raddul Fitna 3. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the slain terrorists, it reported. “The operations severely damaged the khawarij network and restricted their movement,” Pakistan TV said. Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists. The latest operations by the security forces in Balochistan take place as the province continues to face security challenges. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on July 31, the security situation deteriorated most significantly in Balochistan in the country last month. The overall death toll increased by 241pc in Balochistan, from 109 in June to 372 in July, the report said. Security personnel deaths in Balochistan increased from six in June to 62 in July, representing a rise of 933pc. Terrorist deaths rose from 75 to 238, while civilian deaths increased by 93pc, from 28 to 54. Eighteen members of peace committees were also killed in the province. Last month, security forces and law enforcement personnel jointly launched Operation Shaban in Balochistan in retaliation for a deadly attack on a police post at the Mangi Dam pumping station in Ziarat on July 6. During that assault, armed attackers kidnapped and killed 27 police officers . On July 9, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said that the country’s civil and military leadership had taken a “mutual and singular decision ” to end terrorism after multiple major terrorist incidents in Balochistan. He made the remarks at a meeting in Quetta of the Provincial Apex Committee on the National Action Plan , with Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir also present.

items.title: Importations de services : l’Algérie fixe la liste des prestations soumises au PPI
items.description: L’Algérie continue de prendre des mesures pour renforcer le contrôle sur les importations afin de préserver les réserves de change, mais surtout encourager la production nationale. Les dernières mesures en date concernent les importations de services dont les formalités sont effectuées exclusivement en ligne depuis le 1 er août via une plateforme dédiée. À l’occasion de ce passage au 100 % numérique pour le dépôt de demandes, le ministère du Commerce extérieur et de la Promotion extérieur a précisé les importations de services soumises au Programme prévisionnel d’importation (PPI) et qui nécessitent donc une autorisation préalable et obligatoire de son département pour la domiciliation bancaire. Salaires des joueurs étrangers, dividendes… : ces prestations sont soumises au PPI Parmi les activités soumises au PPI services figurent le renouvellement de licences, l’acquisition et la mise à jour de logiciels, le consulting, les frais de formation, le transfert des dividendes, les frais de participation aux évènements à l’étranger, les franchises, les honoraires de bureaux d’études, les joueurs et staffs techniques étrangers, le transfert des salaires des expatriés, la part transférables des appels d’offres internationaux, les cotisations, les excédents de recette et les services juridiques. La plateforme précise que d’autres services sont soumis au PPI. Ce dispositif de contrôle des importations a été instauré par le ministère du Commerce extérieur et de la Promotion des exportations en juillet 2025, avec l’objectif annoncé de renforcer le contrôle sur le commerce extérieur, de lutter contre la fraude notamment via la surfacturation ou la sous-facturation, d’encourager la production nationale et de préserver les réserves de change. Ces mesures ont été prises dans un contexte de forte hausse des importations (biens et services) qui ont atteint 63,4 milliards de dollars en 2025 contre 54,62 milliards en 2024, 49,46 milliards en 2023, 46,02 milliards en 2022, 43,56 milliards en 2021 et 40,98 milliards en 2020. Cette hausse des importations est due principalement aux investissements publics dans les grands projets d’infrastructures de base et aux acquisitions d’équipements opérées par l’Algérie depuis la fin du Covid-19 comme la construction de la ligne ferroviaire entre Béchar et le gisement de minerai de fer de Gara Djebilet sur 950 km, le chantier de la voie ferrée entre le gisement de phosphate de Blad el Hadba à Tébessa et le port d’Annaba, la modernisation de ce dernier, et l’achat de plusieurs avions neufs pour Air Algérie. items.title: Nasarawa Govt to collaborate with Colombia on counterterrorism
items.description: The Nasarawa State Government says it is strengthening ties with the Colombian Government on peacebuilding to help prevent violent extremism in the state. Gov. Abdullahi Sule stated this while hosting a Colombian delegation and officials of the National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) at the Government House in Lafia, the state capital. The visit was part of a field mission aimed at sharing experience in reintegration, reconciliation and the inclusion of women in peacebuilding efforts across the state. Receiving the delegation, Sule said Nasarawa was aware of the challenges Colombia had faced in the past and commended the country for overcoming them. He said Nasarawa stood to benefit from Colombia’s experience and urged the visiting team to share lessons that would deepen peace efforts across the state. Sule directed relevant ministries, departments and agencies to take part in a two-day workshop to cascade the knowledge gained, in line with a train-the-trainer approach proposed by the visiting team. The Director, Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism at NCTC, Amb. Abimbola Wonosikou, said the field mission was part of Nigeria’s partnership with Colombia under the South-South Cooperation (SSC) initiative. Wonosikou said Nasarawa was selected for the mission because of its unique security context. The Colombian delegation leader, Mariana Hernández, said the team was in Nasarawa to share experience with and learn from participants at the workshop. She described the exercise as part of the broader South-South Cooperation effort between Nigeria and Colombia. Hernández commended Sule for approving the hosting of the workshop on women in leadership and as partners in peacebuilding. She also said the workshop was designed to empower 80 women affected by various forms of violent extremism in the state. items.title: 2 African countries qualify for 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup
items.description: Algeria and Morocco have become the first African nations to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil after both secured victories in their Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) quarter-finals. Algeria booked their place at the global tournament for the first time after coming from behind to beat Côte d’Ivoire 2-1, while Morocco defeated defending champions South Africa by the same scoreline. The two North African sides secured automatic qualification by reaching the WAFCON semi-finals. Algeria produced a dramatic comeback against Côte d’Ivoire after Ines Konan put the Ivorians ahead in the 30th minute. The Fennecs were handed a major boost before half-time when Côte d’Ivoire were reduced to 10 players following N’Sira Ouedraogo’s dismissal for a high boot on goalkeeper Chloe N’Gazi. Algeria took advantage after the break, with Ines Khiri restoring parity in the 58th minute with a looping effort over goalkeeper Aramatou Diakite. Six minutes later, Amira Braham completed the turnaround with a long-range strike into the bottom-right corner to send Algeria into their first-ever Women’s World Cup finals. Morocco also secured their second successive World Cup appearance after edging South Africa 2-1. The Atlas Lionesses took the lead in the 29th minute when Sakina Ouzraoui produced a superb first-time lob over South Africa goalkeeper Kaylin Swart. Morocco doubled their advantage shortly after half-time when Hanane Ait El Haj converted from the penalty spot after Noxolo Cesane brought down Ghizlane Chebbak. South Africa responded through Thembi Kgatlana in the 67th minute, but Morocco held on to reach the semi-finals and secure their place at Brazil 2027. Morocco made history at the 2023 Women’s World Cup by becoming the first Arab nation to reach the knockout stages of the competition. Two more African nations will join Algeria and Morocco at the 2027 World Cup after the remaining WAFCON quarter-finals. Cameroon face Nigeria, while Malawi take on Ghana on Sunday, with both winners automatically securing World Cup qualification. Côte d’Ivoire and South Africa, meanwhile, remain in contention through the FIFA Play-Off Tournament. The two defeated quarter-finalists will meet in a play-off match on 13 August, with the winner advancing to the 2027 World Cup alongside one of the other two losing quarter-finalists. The 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup will be staged in Brazil, with the tournament bringing together the world’s leading women’s national teams. items.title: Iran issues demands for reopening of Hormuz
items.description: Iran set preconditions on Saturday for a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, including compensation for war damages, complicating a potential deal to open the waterway essential to the world economy. Tehran has imposed an effective blockade of the strait since the United States and Israel struck Iran in late February, and wants to charge tolls for passage, attacking ships it accuses of attempting to circumvent its preferred route. Continued attacks in the strait, which was free to transit before the war, led to the collapse of an April ceasefire. Mediators have since urged both sides to return to the terms of a June memorandum. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said discussions with Oman over transit and management of the strait were “approaching the final stages”, but added the reopening of Hormuz “is subject to other conditions and compensation for the violation” of the June agreement. Security chief Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr on Saturday laid out a list of demands for reopening the strait, including an end to the “war and aggression against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen, and Iraq”. He also demanded the lifting of a parallel US naval blockade of Iran, the end of sanctions, the release of frozen assets and compensation for wartime damage, according to remarks reported by Tasnim news agency. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, meanwhile, said Hormuz’s reopening had “nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman”, adding that the “enemy is forced to accept Iran’s conditions for the opening of the strait”. – Repeated attacks – The comments came as transit through Hormuz has dropped significantly, with Iran targeting ships it accuses of skirting its preferred route through Iranian waters. The United Arab Emirates’ foreign ministry on Saturday condemned what it called a “hostile Iranian attack that targeted a tanker belonging to ADNOC (Abu Dhabi National Oil Company) with a missile while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz, without causing casualties”. Later on Saturday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said a ship was hit by a projectile off Oman in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire that was extinguished but no casualties. It was unclear whether they were referring to the same ship. On Friday, ADNOC had put out a statement saying that since the start of the war, 15 of its vessels had been attacked in Hormuz, “including three vessels this week alone”. Oman’s foreign ministry on Saturday condemned “repeated attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz”, without naming Iran. It also said that “ongoing negotiations regarding navigation arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz are proceeding in a positive and constructive atmosphere”, and urged against any actions that might jeopardise the progress. The previous Iran-US deal — meant to serve as a jumping-off point for negotiations on a permanent settlement — had said Iran and Oman would hash out future arrangements for the strait in discussion with other Gulf countries and “in line with the applicable international law”. International law generally forbids tolling in such waterways. – Security agreement – Turkey’s foreign minister said Saturday he expected Egypt to join a joint defence agreement between Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan designed to stabilize the region, calling the country a “natural partner on all issues”. “I believe that at the next stage Egypt will also be among us in the alliance. We already act toward one another as if we were alliance members,” Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said in an interview. A drone struck US assets at an Egyptian port on the Mediterranean last month, marking the first drone attack on Egyptian territory since the outbreak of the Iran war. Fidan said the agreement does not target a specific country. “There is no common threat that we have put in writing,” he said, according to the news agency. Pakistan’s foreign ministry said Friday the pact meant an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all, adding it was “intended to strengthen collective deterrence”. bur-aya/jsa/smw/lga/tc The post Iran issues demands for reopening of Hormuz appeared first on Vanguard News .

La première affiche opposera le Cameroun au Nigeria, à partir de 18h au Stade Larbi Zaouli à Casablanca, avec à la clé une place dans le dernier carré et un duel à venir face aux Lionnes de l’Atlas. Les deux rencontres de ce dimanche permettront donc de connaître les quatre demi-finalistes de cette CAN féminine 2026, également qualificative pour la Coupe du monde féminine, prévue au Brésil du 24 juin au 25 juillet 2027. items.title: JAMB Registrar clears 5,000 complaints in five days, takes SERVICOM reforms to candidates
items.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has said its new Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, personally intervened in the resolution of more than 5,000 pending complaints within five days. The development followed Aina’s decision to relocate his office to the Board’s Service Compact with All Nigerians (SERVICOM) Unit, where he reviewed complaints from candidates and other clients of the examination body. The Board’s Acting Director of Public Affairs and Protocol, Dr Fabian Benjamin, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the intervention was part of the Registrar’s efforts to improve service delivery to JAMB candidates and other clients. According to Benjamin, Aina has made “Service at Heart” the second of the five enduring pillars of his administration, reflecting a focus on improving the Board’s responsiveness to candidates. The Registrar also directed SERVICOM Desk Officers to adopt a holistic approach to complaints and ensure that genuine cases were addressed promptly instead of being allowed to accumulate. The Board said more than 5,000 pending complaints were consequently resolved within five days. The complaints covered issues encountered by candidates during registration, examination, admission and other JAMB-related processes. Among the cases addressed were difficulties faced by candidates trying to generate profile codes after losing access to telephone numbers used for previous registrations. The intervention also covered biometric verification challenges, including cases involving candidates who experienced biometric failures during registration or the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME). Aina also reviewed complaints relating to the Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS), including cases involving candidates who lost their phones or SIM cards, candidates who changed from Direct Entry (DE) to UTME, and graduates whose names were missing from the National Matriculation List. Other complaints resolved included payment-related issues, examination venue concerns, e-PIN challenges, technical difficulties and problems relating to the uploading of documents. The Board also attended to requests involving corrections to names, dates of birth, states of origin and local government areas. Benjamin said the Registrar’s presence at the SERVICOM Unit enabled him to directly review complaints and identify issues affecting their resolution. The exercise, according to the Board, is part of Aina’s broader efforts to improve the experience of candidates and other members of the public who interact with JAMB. The Board said the intervention would support efforts to make its complaint-resolution process more responsive and accessible to candidates. items.title: Tunisie – Algérie | Non à la spoliation, à l’intimidation et à la vassalisation !
items.description: À la demande pressante d’amis chers et de confrères dont le patriotisme commande le respect, il convient aujourd’hui — à contre-cœur et en me pinçant très fort le nez — de descendre dans l’arène. L'objectif est de dissiper le tissu de contes de fées et de contre-vérités crasses que le soi-disant Dr Abderrahmane Cherfouh a commis dans les colonnes de Kapitalis pour tenter de faire taire la critique et de délégitimer mes analyses sur les relations tuniso-algériennes. ** Elyes Kasri * Ce texte de la plume indigeste du Dr Cherfouh ne relève ni de la réflexion ni du débat d'idées, mais d'une tentative de voltige informationnelle assez pathétique. Accuser un diplomate tunisien de «diaboliser» l’Algérie parce qu’il dissèque les leviers d’influence d’un pays voisin est un procédé d'intimidation intellectuelle usé jusqu'à la corde. Passer au scalpel les impostures de ce censeur d’opérette permet de trancher dans le vif d'une relation bilatérale que certains tentent de faire avaler sous perfusion sentimentale. 1- L’imposture morale : avant d’ausculter la souveraineté tunisienne, Dr Chelfouh, en mal de reconnaissance, devrait interroger son effroyable désertion morale. Voilà un clinicien qui a choisi de s'installer confortablement au Canada, fuyant la misère politique et économique de son propre pays pour aller soigner les rhumes à Montréal. En s’exilant pour son confort personnel, il a délibérément choisi de priver ses concitoyens de ses prétendus talents, foulant aux pieds le serment d’Hippocrate avec un cynisme consommé. C’est depuis son exil doré, bien au chaud à des milliers de kilomètres, que Dr Cherfouh s’improvise général en chef du patriotisme maghrébin. Son indignation sélective et sa sémantique, si lourdement calquée sur les communiqués de presse des officines de la Mouradia, trahissent sa véritable fonction : celle de prête-nom pour la propagande d’un régime militaire aux abois. La plume du Dr Cherfouh n’est pas guidée par la fraternité, elle est simplement téléguidée. Le public tunisien refuse de recevoir des ordonnances géopolitiques d’un expatrié qui a troqué son stéthoscope contre les basses œuvres de la guerre psychologique régionale. 2- La nature prédatrice de la junte d’Alger : Dr Cherfouh tente de draper la junte d’Alger dans les vertus de la fraternité maghrébine. La réalité politique est une insulte à ce concept. L’Algérie est gouvernée par une oligarchie militaire prédatrice, une gérontocratie de généraux à médailles qui maintient son propre peuple sous une chape de plomb d’un autre âge, étouffe l’expression populaire, embastille les journalistes au moindre mot et a totalement assassiné l’élan démocratique du Hirak. Ce paternalisme de caserne, où un régime despotique, liberticide et corrompu se pique de donner des leçons de morale et de bon voisinage par l’intermédiaire du soi-disant Dr Chelfouh, est d’un comique absolu. Au-delà de la farce rhétorique, il faut appeler les choses par leur nom : le régime militaire d’Alger s’est érigé en principale menace contre les aspirations démocratiques, de justice sociale et de progrès du peuple tunisien. En exportant son modèle autocratique et liberticide par un chantage permanent, la Mouradia cherche activement à étouffer le pluralisme tunisien. Ce pouvoir gérontocratique ne peut tolérer l’émergence d’une véritable démocratie moderne et progressiste à ses portes, de peur qu’elle ne serve d’exemple à une jeunesse algérienne opprimée. Saboter le progrès institutionnel et social de la Tunisie est une stratégie de survie pour cette junte kleptocrate. Un régime qui traite ses propres citoyens en sujets terrorisés n’a aucune légitimité pour venir dicter les frontières de la liberté d’expression ou des analyses diplomatiques en Tunisie. Que ces messieurs les généraux balaient d’abord les cours de leurs propres prisons avant de vouloir régenter l’esprit critique tunisien. De plus, de la «décennie noire» aux maquis du GSPC et d’Aqmi, Alger a toujours utilisé la porosité terroriste transfrontalière comme un bouton de pression politique pour forcer Tunis à l’alignement. 3- Le chantage au Transmed ou le paradoxe d’un cordon ombilical vital : l’arrogance d’Alger atteint son paroxysme lorsque, par la voix du Dr Cherfouh, elle présente le transit du gaz comme une «faveur» ou une obole charitable accordée à la Tunisie. C’est un contresens économique absolu. Le régime algérien est en situation de faillite systémique sur tous les plans. Il ne survit artificiellement que grâce à la rente des hydrocarbures, dont une part majeure transite par le gazoduc Transmed via le sol tunisien pour alimenter l’Italie. Le Transmed n’est pas une fleur faite à la Tunisie ; c’est le ballon d’oxygène vital de la Mouradia, la laisse énergétique sans laquelle le budget de l’État algérien s’effondrerait instantanément. Et pourtant, par un renversement burlesque des réalités, Alger utilise ce tuyau indispensable à sa propre survie comme une arme de chantage pour vassaliser la Tunisie. Ce piratage commercial s'appuie sur une spoliation tarifaire évidente : 1 – une redevance tunisienne dérisoire de 5,25 %. Pour 400 kilomètres d’infrastructures lourdes qui hypothèquent le territoire national, la Tunisie ne perçoit qu’une maigre redevance, un taux dérisoire bloqué par les menaces d’Alger depuis des décennies; 2- le modèle souverain du Maroc : à titre de comparaison, sur l’ancien gazoduc GME, le Maroc avait imposé un taux de 7 % à 10 % des volumes, assorti du transfert de la propriété intégrale des installations à l’État marocain après 25 ans. Autant dire qu’à Alger, on sait compter quand il s’agit d’exploiter les voisins à vil prix, tout en se permettant de menacer de fermer les vannes à la moindre velléité d’indépendance diplomatique et d’expression des aspirations démocratiques de la Tunisie. La diplomatie n’est pas une affaire de sensiblerie mémorielle ni de slogans lénifiants comme le «khawa-khawa» bon pour les naïfs. La Tunisie n’a besoin ni de la protection étouffante ni des conseils d’un pays en faillite systémique qui ne produit rien d’autre que du ressentiment. En analysant lucidement les risques de cette dépendance structurelle, les observateurs indépendants font leur strict devoir d’expertise et de patriotisme. Les valets d’influence de la Mouradia, qu’ils écrivent masqués derrière la fausse identité du soi-disant Dr Cherfouh depuis son exil doré et pantouflard au Canada ou à découvert, doivent comprendre que la Tunisie n’est pas et ne sera jamais la 70 e wilaya algérienne. Surtout qu’elle a toujours, tout au long de son histoire plusieurs fois millénaire, gouverné ce territoire voisin à partir de Carthage, Dougga, Kairouan, Mahdia et Tunis. Le droit à la liberté d’opinion et d’analyse géopolitique restera libre, souverain et totalement imperméable aux intimidations des censeurs d’Alger ou d’ailleurs. Un vieux proverbe tunisien dit :.ما دواء الفم الابخر كان السواك الحار * Ancien ambassadeur. ** La rédaction : avec cette réponse, on clos ce débat qui ne saurait s'éterniser. items.title: Vaste feu de forêt dans l'ouest du Canada: 20.000 évacués, état d'urgence
items.description: Plus de 20.000 personnes ont été évacuées depuis vendredi dans la province canadienne de Colombie-Britannique (ouest) en raison d'un important feu de forêt qui se propage rapidement, ont indiqué les autorités qui ont déclaré l'état d'urgence. Des vents ont attisé l'incendie de Bald Range près du lac Okanagan au sud de la Colombie-Britannique, qui a pris rapidement de l'ampleur et a déjà ravagé plus de 10.000 hectares, touchant les populations des vallées environnantes. « Nous savons qu'il y a eu des pertes importantes de maisons et de biens. Nous savons aussi que certaines personnes se sont retrouvées piégées, les conditions ayant changé très rapidement », a déclaré le Premier ministre de la Colombie-Britannique, David Eby, dans un communiqué samedi soir, ajoutant que « des évacuations aériennes sont en cours pour des personnes qui sont conservées isolées » par l'incendie. Selon CTV News, plus de 50 personnes ont dû être évacuées par voie aérienne de la localité de Faulder à mesure que les flammes avançaient. Kelly Greene, ministre provinciale de la Gestion des situations d'urgence et de la Préparation aux changements climatiques, a déclaré l'état d'urgence. Les trois dernières saisons des feux ont été parmi les plus destructrices jamais enregistrées au Canada, vaste pays qui se réchauffe deux fois plus rapidement que le reste de la planète. Le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney a salué sur X les pompiers du pays qui travaillent « inlassablement pour assurer la sécurité des citoyens » . Thousands of people in Summerland, B.C., are being evacuated as intense wildfires threaten their community. To the brave firefighters and first responders working tirelessly to keep people safe: thank you. The federal government stands ready to help and support the Government… — Mark Carney (@MarkJCarney) August 8, 2026 « Le gouvernement fédéral est prêt à aider et à soutenir le gouvernement de la Colombie-Britannique dans ces efforts. Mes pensées vont à toutes les personnes qui ont été forcées de quitter leur domicile et j'espère qu'elles pourront y retourner saines et sauvées rapidement », a déclaré Carney. L'incendie a été signalé pour la première fois tôt vendredi soir, et Eby a averti samedi qu'il « reste extrêmement actif et que d'importants défis subsistent ». Abritant plus d'un quart des forêts boréales mondiales, dont près de 40% sont non-aménagées – c'est-à-dire laissées à leur état naturel – le Canada n'a pas les moyens humains et matériels d'éteindre l'ensemble de ces feux et concentre ses efforts sur la protection des zones peuplées, notamment par des populations autochtones. The post Vaste feu de forêt dans l'ouest du Canada: 20.000 évacués, état d'urgence appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Peter Obi advocates leadership measured by impact on lives
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 election, Mr Peter Obi, has advocated leadership that is measured by its visible impact on the lives of citizens. Obi, who was the special guest of honour at an empowerment programme organised by the member representing Awka North and South Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Prof. Lilian Orogbu, commended the lawmaker for what he described as purposeful and people-oriented representation. At the event, Orogbu empowered more than 500 constituents with cars, shuttle buses, tricycles, motorcycles, sewing machines, grinding machines, deep freezers and 1KVA and 2KVA generating sets, among other items. Scholarships were also awarded to selected students as part of the lawmaker’s efforts to support access to education in the constituency. Obi said initiatives such as the empowerment programme could help improve livelihoods, reduce poverty and contribute to addressing social challenges. He expressed concern over unemployment, challenges in the education and healthcare sectors and insecurity in the country, attributing many of the challenges to poor governance and the management of public resources. Reaffirming his vision for Nigeria, Obi said competent and accountable leadership could help the country address hunger, insecurity, unemployment and economic hardship. He also called for credible elections in 2027, urging Nigerians to reject electoral malpractice and uphold the principles of equity, justice and fairness. Speaking at the event, Orogbu said the empowerment programme was organised to appreciate her supporters, volunteers and constituents who supported her during the 2023 general elections. She said more than 36,000 people voted for her, while over 5,000 supporters participated actively in her campaign. Orogbu, however, noted that it would be difficult to accommodate everyone in a single phase of the programme, adding that another round of empowerment had been scheduled for November 2026. She urged the beneficiaries to make productive use of the items, saying the initiative was intended not only as welfare support but also as an intervention to improve livelihoods, create employment opportunities and support families across Awka North and South Federal Constituency. She said sustainable empowerment could contribute to poverty reduction, address youth unemployment and stimulate grassroots economic development. The Anambra State Chairman of the NDC, Hon. Ikem Uzoezie, congratulated Orogbu on what he described as her efforts to fulfil campaign promises through constituency representation. He urged residents to continue supporting the party, expressing optimism that sustained electoral support would lead to more development projects and improved welfare. Also speaking, the Senator representing Anambra Central, Chief Victor Umeh, described Orogbu as a valuable representative of the people of Awka North and South Federal Constituency. Umeh said the lawmaker had distinguished herself through constituency projects, scholarships, infrastructure initiatives and empowerment programmes. He also commended her contributions on the floor of the House of Representatives, saying they had helped draw attention to the needs of the constituency. Umeh urged constituents to support Orogbu’s bid for a second term, saying her return to the House could make her a ranking member and potentially enhance her capacity to attract development to the constituency. He described the empowerment programme as significant and said it reflected Orogbu’s efforts to support her constituents. The post Peter Obi advocates leadership measured by impact on lives appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Defence Minister unveils ‘New Face of Alaba’, hails market’s growth
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Minister of Defence, Gen. Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), has commended the transformation of Alaba International Market, describing it as an example of Nigerian enterprise, innovation and economic resilience. Musa spoke at the gala and award night marking the unveiling of the “New Face of Alaba” in Ikoyi, Lagos, where he acknowledged the market’s development as a major centre for electronics and technology. The minister said the newly commissioned commercial complexes represented more than physical development, noting that they reflected the vision and efforts of the Alaba business community. He congratulated the leadership of the International Market Association Electronics (IMAE), particularly its President-General, High Chief Dr Camilus Nnamdi Amajuoyi, as well as the Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, for their contributions to the market’s transformation. Musa said Alaba International Market had evolved beyond its traditional role as a marketplace to become an important contributor to economic activity, employment and technological development. He also highlighted efforts within the market to promote quality assurance, encourage locally manufactured products and tackle counterfeit goods, saying such measures would strengthen confidence in the market. The minister reiterated the Federal Government’s commitment to providing a secure and conducive environment for businesses to operate. He also commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for his administration’s focus on national security and economic stability, stressing the importance of collaboration among government, businesses and citizens in promoting sustainable development. Musa urged traders, manufacturers and entrepreneurs in the Alaba community to sustain their commitment to innovation, integrity and excellence. According to a statement by the Ministry of Defence Public Relations Officer, Capt. Moses Yare, the minister encouraged members of the business community to maintain standards that would enhance Nigeria’s competitiveness while creating opportunities for future generations. The event also featured the recognition of individuals whose contributions have supported the development of Alaba International Market. Musa congratulated the Alaba business community on the milestone and expressed optimism about further development of the market. In his remarks, Lagos State Governor Sanwo-Olu, represented by his deputy, Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, commended the Alaba International Market community for its contribution to the state’s economy. Hamzat said the market remained important to commerce, innovation and employment generation, while commending the resilience and enterprise of its traders. He reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to reconstructing the road linking Alaba International Market, saying the project would improve accessibility, ease business activities and support economic growth in the area. The statement also noted that the IMAE had maintained a longstanding relationship with the Nigerian Army spanning several decades, adding that the relationship was facilitated by Musa when he was a young army officer. The post Defence Minister unveils ‘New Face of Alaba’, hails market’s growth appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Army rescues 33 kidnapped passengers in Zamfara
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the 1 Brigade, Nigerian Army, Forward Operating Base (FOB) Tsafe, have rescued 33 passengers abducted by terrorists while travelling through Magazu Village in Tsafe Local Government Area of Zamfara State. The Nigerian Army said the rescue operation was conducted at about 8:15 a.m. on August 8, 2026, following credible intelligence on the abduction. According to the Army, the troops swiftly mobilised to the area and made contact with the terrorists, who were moving the abducted passengers to an undisclosed location. The troops engaged the terrorists, forcing them to abandon the passengers and flee into adjoining bushes. The 33 passengers were subsequently rescued and secured by the troops for further necessary action. Following the rescue, the soldiers conducted an exploitation of the surrounding area while pursuing the fleeing terrorists. The Army said no troop casualty was recorded during the operation. The operation, it added, underscores the continued efforts of the Nigerian Army to protect civilians, disrupt terrorist activities and rescue abducted persons along vulnerable routes in Zamfara State. The post Army rescues 33 kidnapped passengers in Zamfara appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Burkina : Le FSP mobilise plus de 700 millions FCFA par mois pour le Bataillon Mixte de Marche Fantôme 1
items.description: Burkina : Le FSP mobilise plus de 700 millions FCFA par mois pour le Bataillon Mixte de Marche Fantôme 1 Fada N'Gourma, 8 août 2026 (AIB) – Le Fonds de soutien patriotique (FSP) mobilise chaque mois plus de 700 millions de FCFA pour assurer le fonctionnement du Bataillon Mixte de Marche Fantôme 1, a indiqué vendredi le secrétaire général du ministère de l'Économie et des Finances, Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama, à l'issue d'une mission d'immersion des membres du Conseil d'orientation (CO) et du Comité de gestion (CG) du FSP. « Chaque franc que l'on injecte dans le Fonds de soutien patriotique contribue à renforcer les capacités opérationnelles de nos VDP et de nos forces de défense et de sécurité sur le terrain », a déclaré M. Soulama, qui conduisait la mission au Bataillon Mixte de Marche Fantôme 1. Cette immersion fait suite à une instruction du Premier ministre Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, président du Conseil d'orientation du FSP. Elle visait à permettre aux membres des deux instances de constater sur le terrain les réalisations rendues possibles grâce aux contributions des Burkinabè. Selon le secrétaire général du ministère de l'Économie et des Finances, plus de 700 millions de FCFA sont consacrés mensuellement à l'entretien des hommes, à la santé, aux primes, à l'alimentation et à la logistique du bataillon. Il a également indiqué que les équipements mis à la disposition de l'unité représentent près d'un milliard de FCFA. « Nous sommes vraiment émerveillés, a-t-il souligné, par les résultats présentés et les efforts consentis pour mobiliser les ressources nécessaires à la mise en place et au renforcement du bataillon ». M. Soulama a par ailleurs relevé que le renforcement des capacités du bataillon se poursuit, notamment avec la formation de plusieurs centaines de Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP). Il a salué le courage et l'engagement des combattants et appelé l'ensemble des Burkinabè à maintenir leur adhésion au FSP. « Il est vraiment plus que nécessaire pour nous de travailler toujours à accompagner ce Fonds de soutien patriotique », a-t-il insisté, réaffirmant l'importance d'une mobilisation citoyenne en faveur de la défense du territoire. La mission a permis aux membres du CO et du CG de mieux apprécier l'impact des ressources du FSP sur les équipements, les infrastructures et le soutien aux combattants. Ils ont réaffirmé leur engagement en faveur d'une gestion rigoureuse, transparente et efficace des ressources mobilisées. Agence d'Information du Burkina BO/Ata
