items.title: Le béton fait de l’ombre aux arbres
items.description: Aux Parcelles assainies, la chaleur est devenue un sujet de conversation quotidien. Entre les arbres qui disparaissent, le béton qui gagne du terrain et les eaux usées qui stagnent dans certaines rues, les habitants décrivent un quartier où l’ombre se fait de plus en plus rare, alors que la Journée nationale de l’arbre est célébrée ce dimanche à Nioro. Aux Parcelles assainies, sur les ruelles, les rares passants accélèrent le pas pour rejoindre une façade ombragée ou un arbre solitaire. Ce mardi 4 août 2026, il fait plus de 30 degrés dans l’une des plus grandes agglomérations du département de Dakar. À 12h, la grisaille a disparu pour laisser la place au soleil, et les refuges deviennent difficiles à trouver. Dans plusieurs concessions, les arbres se comptent désormais sur les doigts d’une main. Là où des manguiers, des filaos, des badamiers ou des cocotiers procuraient autrefois de la fraîcheur, s’élèvent aujourd’hui des murs en béton, des extensions de maisons ou de simples garages. Le paysage s’est minéralisé au fil des années. « Avant, les enfants jouaient sous les arbres. Aujourd’hui, ils restent enfermés parce qu’il fait trop chaud », se plaint Moussa Guèye, un habitant installé depuis plus de 20 à l’Unité 9 des Parcelles assainies. Pour M. Guèye, Dakar perd progressivement son couvert végétal sans que personne ne semble s’en inquiéter. À l’Unité 15, les eaux usées ruissellent le long de la chaussée. Elles stagnent parfois devant les habitations, dégageant des odeurs qui deviennent plus fortes sous l’effet de la chaleur. Les populations expliquent que l’absence d’arbres aggrave encore cette sensation d’étouffement. « Quand il y avait plus de verdure, la chaleur était supportable. Aujourd’hui, le béton renvoie toute la chaleur », déplore Amina Thioune, une mère de famille faisant la lessive devant sa modeste demeure. À côté, sous un maigre arbre, quelques hommes cherchent un peu d’ombre. Ils observent les immeubles qui remplacent progressivement les espaces libres. « Chaque fois qu’une maison est construite, c’est souvent un arbre qui disparaît. On construit, mais on ne replante pas », regrette Pathé Bâ qui joue en même temps au damier. Le constat revient dans presque toutes les conversations. Les habitants disent comprendre les besoins de logement, mais s’interrogent sur l’absence d’équilibre entre urbanisation et préservation des arbres. « On ne peut pas vivre uniquement avec du ciment », lance l’ancien pêcheur Amsatou Mané, tout en essuyant la sueur qui coule sur son front. Pour de nombreux riverains, cette transformation modifie aussi les habitudes de vie. Les rencontres de voisinage deviennent plus rares en journée. Ainsi, plusieurs enfants attendent la tombée de la nuit pour sortir. Quant aux personnes âgées, elles restent confinées à l’intérieur des maisons. « Avant, on passait du temps dehors. Maintenant, à midi, personne ne peut rester sous le soleil», s’alarme Ndèye Sène, ménagère. Dans ce quartier en pleine densification, plusieurs habitants plaident pour un vaste programme de reboisement urbain. Ils souhaitent que chaque nouvelle construction s’accompagne de plantations et que les espaces publics retrouvent des arbres capables d’offrir de l’ombre. 1,4 million de plants réalisés en 2025 à Dakar À Dakar, l’arbre tente de résister face à l’avancée du béton. La campagne nationale de reboisement 2025 a enregistré des résultats importants dans la région, selon le bilan de la Direction des Eaux et forêts, chasse et de la conservation des sols (Defccs). « La capitale a produit 1.402.969 plants à travers 56 pépinières sur un objectif fixé à 1.530.000 plants, soit un taux de réalisation de 91,70 % », décline le rapport. Dans le détail, Dakar a réalisé 17,98 hectares de plantations massives avec 7.430 plants mis en terre. Ces opérations ont concerné plusieurs sites destinés à renforcer la couverture végétale de la capitale. À cela s’ajoutent 19,93 kilomètres de plantations linéaires, correspondant à 7.696 plants installés le long des axes routiers, dans les alignements urbains, les haies vives ou encore les brise-vent. « L’arbre en ville joue un rôle essentiel dans la lutte contre les effets du changement climatique. Il contribue à réduire les températures, à améliorer la qualité de l’air et à offrir des espaces plus agréables aux populations », expliquent les acteurs du secteur forestier. La restauration des espaces dégradés constitue également un axe majeur. Dakar affiche 40,14 hectares restaurés ou réhabilités, avec 17.520 plants, principalement dans des opérations d’enrichissement végétal. Pour les Eaux et forêts, cette approche permet de « renforcer les espaces existants et de préserver les derniers îlots verts de la région ». B. G. DIOP

Kristo Asafo Mission reaffirms Nana Kwadwo Safo Akofena I as new leader
items.description: The Kristo Asafo Mission of Ghana has reaffirmed Nana Kwadwo Safo Akofena I as the new leader of the church following the death of its founder, Apostle Emeritus Dr Kwadwo Safo Kantanka. The Mission said his selection was carried out by the council of elders in line with the succession arrangement left by the late founder. The reaffirmation was made during a National Joint Intercessory Prayer Service held to honour Apostle Emeritus Dr Kwadwo Safo Kantanka as part of activities marking his birth month. The service, held under the theme “Intercessory Prayer to Mark the Birth Month of Our Founder As He Rests in His Glory”, brought together members of the Mission to remember the founder and pray for the continued progress of the church. The Mission explained that the founder had provided guidance on who should take over the leadership of the church in the event of his death. According to the arrangement, the council was required to select one of his three sons to lead the Mission. Speaking at the prayer service, the Public Relations Officer of the Kristo Asafo Mission of Ghana, Akwesi Ofori, said the council carefully considered the succession process before settling on Nana Kwadwo Safo Akofena I. “When you look into the books, the founder mentioned that when he is not around, the council of the church should select any of his three sons to be the leader of the church,” he said. Mr Ofori said the decision was reached after careful deliberations, acknowledging that choosing a new leader was not an easy task for the council. “I think the council did very well. Selecting the new leader was not an easy task for the council. But with good counsel, they were able to come out with Nana Kwadwo Safo Akofena I,” he said. He urged members of the Mission to rally behind the new leader and support his vision for the continued growth of the church. “We are gathered here with our new leader, and he is the one we must listen to and follow through with his vision for the church,” Mr Ofori said.

items.title: Egypt could join Pak-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact once technical issues resolved, says Turkish foreign minister
items.description: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Saturday he believed Egypt could join a defence pact signed between Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia once several technical issues were resolved. “Egypt is already our natural partner on all issues. I believe that at the next stage, Egypt will also be among us in the alliance. We already act toward one another as if we were alliance members. There are a few technical issues. Once these are implemented, there is no reason for Egypt not to be part of it,” he told Turkiye’s state-run Anadolu news agency. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed in the Saudi city on Friday, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers the three states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. Fidan said other countries had expressed interest in joining the agreement, but the founding members had debated how the expansion should be handled. Some countries that wanted to join asked not to be named, he said, adding that the preferred model was for Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to remain the three core founding countries, responsible for establishing the principles, standards and long-term structure of the alliance, while other countries could join with the approval of the core members. “Under our president’s vision, we should not remain limited to three countries. We should grow,” Fidan said. Fidan also said the initiative was broader than the traditional definition of the Middle East because of Pakistan’s participation. Pakistan’s geographical position meant the initiative went beyond the conventional definition of the Middle East and represented a broader regional perspective. ‘Same as Nato’s Article 5’ Fidan further elaborated on this, saying the pact was technically the same as Nato’s Article 5 mutual defence agreement. Article 5 of the North Atlantic alliance specifies that an attack on one ​of its members is an attack on all of them. It obliges allies to take action they deem necessary to assist the country under attack, including potentially the use of military force. While the Makkah defence pact stipulates the same, Fidan explained that its text contained general commitments whose practical implementation would depend on discussions and decisions by relevant bodies. A country would need to make a request for assistance and would determine the type of support it needs, he said, adding that the requests could be of different kinds, ranging from intelligence and logistics to ammunition or, if necessary, military units, depending on the scale of the threat. The signatories, he said, would decide through consultations what degree, form, and format of ​support they would ask for in the event of an attack, but that no country would be considered a ​threat as long as a member state is not attacked. Fidan also said that the new alliance was not directed against Iran or any other country, but rather served as a general pledge to support the three signatories’ security. He further told Anadolu that discussions on the initiative began before the current war environment, when there was no US-Israel war on Iran and other regional countries had also been involved in the talks leading to the agreement. Fidan said its signatories were countries that did not have expansionist policies. “They are countries concerned with their own borders, their own problems and their development, and, if possible, they want to contribute positively to their environment through good relations and good neighborliness.“ The three countries, he said, had different styles and capacities, but when brought together, they naturally formed a defence-oriented organisation rather than an offensive one. “It is not an approach of going on the offensive and saying, ‘Let’s do this or that together.’ Therefore, unless it is attacked by a country, whether from inside or outside the region, this alliance cannot have any dispute with any country. But, of course, the power composition we have put forward will make a constructive contribution to regional stability,” he said. He termed the pact the “most important step” toward bringing lasting stability to this region. How will the alliance function? According to Fidan, the pact would be operational under a political and military committee comprising foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of general staff, similar to Nato structures. The committee would translate the vision set by the leaders into decisions and carry out related work, while a secretariat would be established to implement those decisions, he explained. “At the first committee meeting, ministers would likely present proposals to the leaders on the establishment, structure and functioning of the secretariat, as well as its initial tasks,” he said, adding that the pact would cover a broad range of military issues, including interoperability, or the ability of countries with different military structures to operate together. Other areas would include joint training, mutual support, logistics, threat assessments, intelligence sharing and, most importantly, defence industry cooperation. He said the committee would meet at certain intervals during the year and that a permanent secretariat would be established in Saudi Arabia. The structure, functioning and additional units of the secretariat would be determined in discussions among the members. Fidan added that joint exercises and training would be necessary to establish the ability of the countries to operate together. “Because after a while you will see that when you find yourselves in a common combat scenario, how your weapons systems and communications systems will communicate with one another and how they will be compatible are important issues. These are the things that will be done after the secretariat is established,” he said. He said standards would need to be developed and that analyses and assessments would also be carried out. ‘Support in the Muslim world and the West’ Fidan said the defence agreement had received strong support from countries in the Muslim world, including those that were not members but were nevertheless very pleased with the agreement. He said there were also supporters in the West who understood the substance of the initiative. “Especially in the Islamic world, there are many who strongly support this issue. There are also supporters in the West, among those who understand the essence of the matter. The way for the Middle East to cease being a place that produces problems for humanity and the international community and instead become a place that creates added value with everything it possesses is through implementing constructive alliances of this kind,” Fidan said. Fidan said the leadership of Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had created significant regional and global expectations and that officials now had the responsibility to fill those expectations professionally. “Our responsibility, in the positions we hold, is to recognise that the political will put forward by the leadership of the three countries has created a very significant regional and global expectation. We need to fill that expectation very professionally, move forward step by step and make it work. We have begun doing this, and God willing, we will continue,” he said.

items.title: Prosecuting politicians does not mean Ghana’s democracy is under attack – Duncan Amoah to NPP
items.description: The Executive Secretary of the Chamber of Petroleum Consumers (COPEC), Duncan Amoah, has dismissed claims that investigations involving politicians and public officials amount to an attack on Ghana’s democracy. He said the scrutiny of former government officials should not automatically be interpreted as political persecution, arguing that accountability remains an important part of a functioning democratic system. His comments come after the New Patriotic Party’s “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration on August 6, 2026, during which the party raised concerns over alleged threats to democratic governance and what it described as the targeting of its members. Mr Amoah said Ghana’s democratic institutions must be allowed to perform their duties, while citizens retain the right to question or criticise the manner in which those institutions operate. “When you have institutions get to work, you don’t have any objection but to sometimes critique the way institutions work. But to lump everything together and say the entire democratic process is under attack, some of us would beg to differ,” he said. He also said he was yet to see a situation in Ghana where an opposition figure was targeted simply for openly expressing political views. “I have not in Ghana seen or come across an opposition element being just vocal and being targeted by government,” he said. Mr Amoah further pointed to freedom of expression as evidence that Ghana’s democratic space remains open, stressing that citizens continue to have the opportunity to voice their opinions on national issues. “Freedom of speech, which is one of the core tenets of democracy, clearly is also not being attacked as we speak. You can speak your mind,” he said. Speaking on Channel One TV on Saturday, August 8, Mr Amoah, however, cautioned political actors against crossing the line from legitimate criticism into threats or intimidation. He said political discourse should allow room for robust criticism while ensuring that statements made by political actors do not threaten individuals or undermine the rule of law.

Duncan Amoah cautions against political threats in Ghana’s democracy
items.description: The Executive Secretary of the Chamber of Petroleum Consumers (COPEC), Duncan Amoah, has cautioned political actors against using veiled threats in Ghana’s political discourse, warning that such rhetoric could undermine democratic accountability. He said suggestions that political opponents would face retaliation when there is a change in government could discourage legitimate investigations and create a culture where public officials fear accountability. The comments follow the New Patriotic Party’s “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration on August 6, 2026, during which the party raised concerns about alleged political persecution and threats to democratic governance. Duncan Amoah, however, disagreed with the suggestion that Ghana’s democracy was currently under attack, arguing that citizens and political parties continued to have the space to express their views and challenge government decisions. “My personal view is no,” he said when asked whether democracy was under attack in Ghana. He however, expressed concern about what he described as an increasing use of subtle threats in political conversations, particularly statements suggesting that those currently in power could face reprisals when the political tide changes. “What is concerning is the growing tendency for subtle threats to enter our political discourse. You see a threat from the opposition that says the tables will turn and we will do things to you. You hear functionaries sometimes issue those threats,” he said. He said such comments could create the impression that investigations into alleged wrongdoing should be halted because those being scrutinised could eventually return to power. “What you are indirectly saying is that even if we did wrong, or adverse findings are made against us, do not go after us because someday you may not be in power,” he stated. Speaking on Citi FM on Saturday, August 8, Mr Amoah said political interests should not be allowed to take precedence over accountability, stressing that the consequences would ultimately be borne by the wider population. “If we allow this country to be governed that way, it is not the NPP or NDC that suffers; it is the people,” he said.

items.title: Céréales : pourquoi l’Algérie continue d’importer du blé, malgré une récolte exceptionnelle
items.description: Alors que l’Algérie s’achemine vers une récolte exceptionnelle de céréales, l’Office algérien des céréales (OAIC) vient de conclure l’achat de 720.000 tonnes de blé tendre . Un achat qui rappelle que la production locale est loin de couvrir la totalité des besoins nationaux, qui s’élèvent à plus de 12 millions de tonnes de céréales. Les chiffres définitifs devraient être connus après le 10 août, soit après la date officielle de fin des moissons . Les nouveaux centres de collecte des CCLS continuent à remonter par voie informatique directement à l’OAIC les quantités de grains engrangés. Céréales : l'Algérie sur la voie de l'autosuffisance en blé dur De son côté, l’USDA, le département américain à l’Agriculture, évoque une production de 3,2 millions de tonnes de blé, en hausse de 7 % par rapport à 2025. Pour l’orge, l’USDA prévoit une récolte de 1,35 million de tonnes d’orge destinées au cheptel ovin, en hausse de 13 %. Pour le maïs, la récolte attendue est de 12.000 tonnes, soit la même que l’année passée, selon le département d’État américain à l’Agriculture. Récemment, Saïd Sayoud, le ministre de l'Intérieur, des Collectivités locales et des Transports, a annoncé une récolte historique totale de 5 millions de tonnes de céréales cette année. Si l’Algérie continue d’importer du blé tendre, qui sert notamment à la fabrication de la farine pour le pain, l'autosuffisance en blé dur, qui est utilisé pour fabriquer la semoule, pourrait être atteinte dès cette année. Dans la mesure où, sur le marché international, le prix du blé dur est en moyenne une fois et demie supérieur à celui du blé tendre, l’économie devrait être de plus de 1,5 milliard de dollars, a estimé le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune lors de sa dernière rencontre avec des représentants de la presse nationale lundi 27 juillet. Historiquement, l’Algérie est un pays de blé dur. Pluie abondante et aide de l’État : les deux facteurs clés de la récolte record de céréales Les bons résultats de cette année sont liés à l’abondance et à l’excellente répartition des pluies. Celles tombées en automne ont été décisives. Elles ont amené les agriculteurs à prolonger les semis et encore en décembre, les CCLS ont vu affluer les agriculteurs à la recherche de semences certifiées. Ces résultats n’auraient pas été possibles sans le soutien multiforme de l’État à la filière. Un soutien qui concerne les semences, les engrais, le matériel, le carburant et les prêts de campagne. Sans l’échelonnement accordé aux agriculteurs touchés par les sécheresses de ces dernières années, à l’Ouest du pays, des agriculteurs n’auraient pas pu emblaver leurs parcelles. Parmi le soutien à la filière figure la réalisation de centres de stockage et de silos, dont le programme a été décidé lors du Conseil des ministres, tenu en décembre 2023, sous la présidence du président de la République. La construction de ces 350 centres de collecte illustre les réserves de productivité dans l’organisation de la filière et les avancées possibles. Ces nouvelles structures ont reçu une très forte adhésion de la part des agriculteurs et des investisseurs situés au Sud. À Mascara, comme dans d’autres wilayas, la construction de silos en béton avance. Selon la Télévision algérienne, les immenses cellules y ont atteint une hauteur de 40 mètres. Collées les unes contre les autres, les 9 cellules construites par l’entreprise Cosider devraient permettre de stocker un million de quintaux de blé. Ces jours-ci, la fin des travaux sur l'un de ces chantiers a été fêtée par un feu d’artifice depuis le haut des installations. Aux silos s’ajoute la logistique déployée au Sud sous la forme de convois de camions et d’engins de récolte. Une technique initiée dès 2024 par Youcef Cheurfa, le précédent ministre de l’Agriculture. « Développer des solutions innovantes » Pour les services agricoles, le défi est de ne pas se satisfaire des résultats d’une année et de faire progresser les rendements pour atteindre 20 à 30 quintaux/hectare dans les wilayas du Nord, et 60 à 70 quintaux/hectare dans les wilayas du Sud. Dès 2023, le ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique a installé un groupe de réflexion et de travail composé d’enseignants-chercheurs algériens. Comme le précise Tarik Hartani, directeur de l’École Nationale Supérieure Agronomique, « ce groupe a été chargé d’élaborer une vision scientifique et prospective destinée à jeter les bases d’un plan stratégique pour le développement durable de la filière céréalière en Algérie. » Pour Tarik Hartani, membre du Conseil national de la sécurité alimentaire et coordinateur de ce comité de réflexion, l’Algérie est « confrontée à l’irrégularité des précipitations, à la perturbation des cycles culturaux, à la dégradation des écosystèmes et à l’érosion continue de la biodiversité agricole ». Aussi, estime-t-il que « la communauté scientifique est appelée à développer des solutions innovantes, fondées sur la recherche, afin d’accompagner la modernisation de l’agriculture et de répondre durablement aux défis environnementaux, alimentaires et économiques auxquels le pays est confronté ». Outre le défi climatique, les céréaliers algériens sont confrontés à l’érosion des marges financières à l’hectare. Les charges de mécanisation restent un poste important. Le coût de la récolte est facturé 7.000 DA/hectare par les entrepreneurs de travaux agricoles privés, contre seulement 6.000 DA par les CCLS. L’intervention récente de l’entreprise publique Agrodrive a permis la mise à disposition des exploitations de matériel de récolte et, à l’automne prochain, de tracteurs pour la campagne de labours et semis. En septembre 2023, à l’occasion de la remise du rapport du comité de réflexion au ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique Kamel Baddari, M. Hartani a indiqué que « le plan stratégique de développement de la production céréalière prévoit également le lancement d’un projet national visant à convertir près de 2,5 millions d’hectares de terres en friche sur une période de dix ans, afin de les consacrer à la production de différentes cultures, y compris les céréale s ». En effet, une partie des terres céréalières reste en jachère (ou repos) une année sur deux et sert au pâturage des moutons. Le défi est donc de trouver les moyens pour que les agriculteurs sèment en sec dès l’automne le maximum de surfaces. Par ailleurs, l’élevage du mouton, qui est une activité complémentaire, ne doit pas se développer au détriment de la culture de céréales. Or, actuellement, à raison de 50-60 DA la botte, contre 20 DA en juin, la paille n’est jamais broyée et enfouie au sol afin de maintenir sa fertilité. En 2026, la Syrie a atteint son autosuffisance en blé. Selon le directeur-adjoint de l'Organisation générale des céréales, Ahmad Qadoun, cité par le site Boursorama : « Il ne sera pas nécessaire d'importer cette saison. » Le Nord-Est du pays, et en particulier la région de Hassaké, a bénéficié d’une aide australienne et développe l’agriculture dite de conservation. Synergie, subventions et techniques modernes En Algérie, la filière céréales bénéficie d’un large soutien public, l’emploi de techniques modernes et la recherche de modes d’organisation nouveaux pourraient permettre une synergie que les subventions seules ne peuvent assurer. En juillet dernier, le professeur Hartani a annoncé dans le quotidien El Watan : « L’inscription officielle de six nouvelles variétés nationales de céréales, dont trois de blé dur et trois d’orge », ce qui constitue « une avancée majeure pour la recherche agronomique algérienne », a-t-il ajouté. Un pas vers cette synergie tant espérée. L’article Céréales : pourquoi l’Algérie continue d’importer du blé, malgré une récolte exceptionnelle est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Burkina : L’hôpital Bogodogo célèbre le premier anniversaire des quintuplés nés dans ses services
items.description: Burkina-Santé-Quintuplés-Don Burkina : L’hôpital Bogodogo célèbre le premier anniversaire des quintuplés nés dans ses services Ouagadougou, 8 août 2026 (AIB) – Le Centre hospitalier universitaire de Bogodogo (CHU-B) a célébré vendredi le premier anniversaire des quintuplés nés dans ses services, en leur offrant des cadeaux et des vivres destinés à soutenir leur prise en charge. Le don, qui s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’accompagnement de la famille par le CHU-B depuis la naissance des cinq enfants, dont trois filles et deux garçons, vise à soutenir leur prise en charge et à témoigner de la solidarité de l’établissement envers la famille. « C’est avec une grande joie que nous disons merci au Seigneur d’avoir donné le don de la vie à ces enfants et de les avoir conduits jusqu’à nos jours sans problème », a déclaré la cheffe du service des affaires sociales du CHU-B, Perpétue Toé. Selon Mme Toé, l’ensemble de l’hôpital, sous l’impulsion de la direction générale, s’est mobilisé dès l’arrivée des quintuplés pour accompagner la famille, aussi bien sur les plans médical que social. La cheffe du service de pédiatrie du CHU-B, Solange Odile Ouédraogo/Yougbaré, s’est réjouie de voir les cinq enfants célébrer leur premier anniversaire en bonne santé, rappelant les difficultés particulières liées aux grossesses multiples, notamment le risque élevé de prématurité. « Ces nouveau-nés sont nés prématurément, mais grâce à l’abnégation et au savoir-faire des services de gynécologie-obstétrique et de néonatologie, ils sont tous vivants à un an et en parfaite santé », a-t-elle indiqué. « Un comité de suivi des enfants a notamment été mis en place. Ce comité effectuait des visites au domicile familial afin de s’assurer des conditions de vie des enfants et du respect de leur suivi médical », a-t-elle expliqué. Elle a également félicité les parents pour leur régularité dans le suivi médical des enfants et les a encouragés à rester attentifs aux signes de danger, notamment la fièvre et le refus de s’alimenter. Pour le père des quintuplés, Boureima Zerbo, cette célébration constitue un moment de « grande joie », d’autant que sa famille continue de bénéficier de l’accompagnement du personnel hospitalier. « Nous ne sommes pas seuls. Il y a toujours des personnes à nos côtés pour veiller sur les enfants », a-t-il témoigné, reconnaissant que la prise en charge simultanée de cinq enfants représente une lourde responsabilité pour les parents. Le père a expliqué que les difficultés liées à l’éducation et aux soins d’un enfant deviennent encore plus complexes lorsqu’il faut s’occuper de cinq enfants en même temps. Depuis l’ouverture du service de pédiatrie du CHU-B en 2017, les équipes médicales ont régulièrement pris en charge des grossesses gémellaires et triples. La naissance des quintuplés constituait toutefois une première pour le service. À travers ce geste, le CHU-B entend renouveler son engagement aux côtés de la famille et rappeler l’importance du suivi médical régulier des nouveau-nés, particulièrement ceux issus de grossesses multiples. En rappel, les quintuplés sont nés dans la nuit du 16 au 17 juillet 2025 au Centre hospitalier universitaire de Bogodogo. Agence d’information du Burkina NO/yos

items.title: Tamale Central MP commemorates Ibrahim Murtala Mohammed’s first death anniversary
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Tamale Central, Prof. Alidu Seidu Mahama, has joined constituents and community members to mark the first anniversary of the death of his predecessor, Dr Ibrahim Murtala Mohammed. The commemoration, held on Saturday, August 8, 2026, included the presentation of food items to widows, orphans and other vulnerable residents in the constituency, followed by Islamic prayers for the late legislator. Prof. Alidu Seidu said the event was organised to honour Dr Murtala Mohammed’s contributions to the constituency and keep alive the values he championed during his time as MP. He announced plans to make the commemoration an annual event, as well as establish a scholarship scheme and an annual memorial lecture in honour of the late legislator. “It’s befitting that we mourn him, we honour him, and we appreciate what he has done for us. We decided to pray for him by reciting the Holy Qur’an and also donate to the widows, orphans, and the downtrodden in our constituency to also join us in praying for him for Allah to give him eternal rest,” he said. Speaking at the event, Prof. Alidu Seidu said the planned initiatives would help preserve Dr Murtala Mohammed’s legacy and continue his commitment to the welfare of constituents. “We are going to institutionalise the commemoration every year. We will institute a scholarship package in his name, as well as an annual memorial lecture in his name. What we are doing today is to demonstrate the commitment he so held dear when he was alive,” he said. The commemoration followed a national inter-faith memorial service held to mark the first anniversary of the August 6, 2025 helicopter crash that claimed the lives of eight people, including Dr Murtala Mohammed. The victims were then Defence Minister Dr Edward Omane Boamah, Dr Ibrahim Murtala Mohammed, Acting Deputy National Security Coordinator Alhaji Limuna Muniru Mohammed, NDC Vice Chairman Dr Samuel Sarpong, former parliamentary candidate Samuel Aboagye, and three Ghana Armed Forces personnel — Squadron Leader Peter Bafemi Anala, Flying Officer Manaen Twum Ampadu and Flight Sergeant Ernest Addo Mensah. The Z-9 helicopter crashed in the Adansi Akrofuom District of the Ashanti Region while travelling from Accra to the region on official duty.

items.title: Mireku Duker questions Mahama Ayariga’s grassroots experience for Local Government Ministry role
items.description: Former Tarkwa MP Mireku Duker has raised questions about whether newly appointed Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs Minister, Mahama Ayariga has sufficient grassroots political experience for the role. Mr Duker acknowledged Mr Ayariga’s extensive experience as a lawyer, parliamentarian and former minister, but argued that managing the Local Government Ministry requires a different set of skills, particularly a strong understanding of local politics and community-level governance. He said the ministry needed a leader who could connect with ordinary Ghanaians and appreciate the realities of local administration. “We need a very local person who resonates,” he said. Mr Duker pointed to his own experience as a former Municipal Chief Executive and a staff member at the Local Government Ministry, saying it had given him an understanding of the ministry’s operations and the challenges associated with local governance. “I’ve been a municipal chief executive before. I’ve worked at the Ministry of Local Government before. So I know how it works, the dynamics of the ministry,” he said. Speaking on Citi FM on Saturday, August 8, 2026, Mr Duker said parliamentary experience alone did not necessarily prepare someone for the demands of grassroots political engagement. “He’s up there as a Member of Parliament who understands the rigours of Parliament, but not necessarily a local politician like Ahmed,” he said, referring to Ibrahim Ahmed, who has been reassigned to the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources. Despite his reservations, Mr Duker praised Mr Ayariga’s competence and described him as a close friend and accomplished lawyer, saying he had confidence in his abilities. “Ayariga is a fine gentleman. He’s really deep. He’s my friend. I know him very well and I can vouch for him,” he said. President John Dramani Mahama announced the latest ministerial appointments and reassignments on Friday, August 7, 2026. Mr Ayariga was appointed Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, while Ibrahim Ahmed was moved to the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources.

items.title: Le poème du dimanche | ‘‘Poème’’ de Samuel Beckett
items.description: Né en 1906 à Cooldrinagh, en Irlande, Samuel Beckett est écrivain, dramaturge et poète. Il écrit en anglais et français. Prix Nobel de littérature, en 1969. Le jour de l'annonce du prix, il était en vacances, incognito, à Hammamet, en Tunisie. Connu surtout pour son théâtre de l’absurde et son œuvre dramatique, pessimiste et non sans dérision, il semble, pourtant, avoir commencé par écrire de la poésie qu’il a publiée très jeune. Il laisse aujourd’hui trois recueils, Peste soit de l’horoscope ; Os d’écho et Poèmes Mirlitornades , paru très peu avant sa mort, en 1989, à Paris, et qui reprend des poèmes écrits vers la fin des années 1930 dont le poème choisi ici. Tahar Bekri bon bon il est un pays où l’oubli où pèse l’oubli doucement sur les mondes innommés là la tête on la tait la tête est muette et on sait non on ne sait rien le chant des bouches mortes meurt sur la grève il a fait le voyage il n’y a rien à pleurer ma solitude je la connais allez je la connais mal j’ai le temps c’est ce que je me dis j’ai le temps mais quel temps os affamé le temps du chien du ciel pâlissant sans cesse mon grain de ciel du rayon qui grimpe ocellé tremblant des microns des années ténèbres Vous voulez que j’aille d’A à B je ne peux pas je ne peux pas sortir je suis dans un pays sans traces oui oui c’est une belle chose que vous avez là une bien belle chose qu’est-ce que c’est ne me posez plus de questions spirale poussière d’instants qu’est-ce que c’est le même le calme l’amour la haine le calme le calme ‘‘Vingt poèmes’’, Ed. Minuit. L’article Le poème du dimanche | ‘‘Poème’’ de Samuel Beckett est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Tinubu’s reforms fuel Nasarawa’s N90bn infrastructure boom – Gov Sule
items.description: Gov. Abdullahi Sule of Nasarawa State says increased revenue from President Bola Tinubu’s reforms has enabled his administration to execute N90 billion worth of infrastructure projects without borrowing from banks. Sule disclosed this at the Government House, Lafia, when he received the Renewed Hope Ambassadors Presidential Media Team, led by Mr Bayo Onanuga, the President’s Special Adviser on Media and Strategy. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the team arrived in Lafia, the state capital, on Saturday to inspect completed and ongoing Federal Government and state infrastructure projects across the state. The governor said the removal of fuel subsidy and other reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had substantially increased the resources available to state governments for infrastructure and development. He explained that Nasarawa’s monthly allocation, previously fluctuating between N3.8 billion and N4.5 billion, had risen to an average of N14 billion to N16 billion. According to Sule, the increased revenue has enabled his administration to execute major infrastructure projects without resorting to bank borrowing. He recalled that Nasarawa previously struggled to raise N5 billion through borrowing for a single market project, but now had the capacity to implement infrastructure valued at about N90 billion without bank loans. He urged other state governments to acknowledge the reforms behind the improved financial resources. “All the projects we are doing in Nasarawa State today, without borrowing from the bank, is as a result of President Bola Tinubu and his support. “So you must give him the credit for that,” he said. Sule admonished journalists that, in discharging their role of holding government accountable for any failure to properly deploy public resources, they should recognise the positive effects of government policies. The governor said the broader purpose of the media tour was to help journalists understand how government policies translated into increased revenues, infrastructure projects, economic opportunities and improvements in citizens’ lives. “It is not just to take pictures of flyovers and pictures of this. No. It’s to understand what is driving these policies,” Sule said. He urged journalists to determine what governors were doing with available resources and how such spending was affecting residents. The governor stressed that objective reporting remained essential to public accountability. According to him, constructive criticism and recognition of positive performance were necessary to strengthen accountability, encourage effective governance and motivate leaders to deliver better results for citizens. NAN reports that the team inspected the Nasarawa State Secretariat, where the Secretary to the State Government, Dr Labaran Magaji (SAN), conducted members round the infrastructure housing about 11 ministries. Magaji said the secretariat was established to consolidate ministries previously operating from scattered and dilapidated offices, following improved revenue accruing to the state through Federation allocations. He said the complex was powered by a one-megawatt solar plant, with the government considering extending excess electricity to neighbouring communities, alongside electric vehicle charging facilities. The team also inspected the Shandam Road and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu Interchange, a N16 billion project, before proceeding towards the Emir’s Palace to assess flood-control works. The inspection further included the Wing Commander Abdullah Ibrahim Skill Acquisition Centre, a state-of-the-art facility used by the Industrial Training Fund and other agencies for skills development and training. The team is scheduled to inspect Avatar Lithium Processing Plant in Nasarawa Local Government Area, described as one of Africa’s major lithium processing facilities. It will also inspect Diamond Energy Lithium Processing Plant, another major facility in Nasarawa Local Government, inaugurated recently by Vice-President Kashim Shettima on behalf of President Tinubu. The inspection will also cover the reconstruction of the Keffi-Nasarawa-Toto-Abaji Road and dualisation of the Keffi-Karu-Abuja Road, alongside a dual overhead bridge easing traffic along the corridor. Earlier, the governor said the twin flyovers in Karu had helped to increase property values around the area, demonstrating how infrastructure could stimulate wider economic benefits beyond improving transportation and reducing traffic congestion. Beyond physical infrastructure, the governor urged journalists to examine Nasarawa’s interventions in healthcare, agriculture and mining. According to him, the sectors were key components of the state’s development strategy. In healthcare, Sule highlighted the expansion of tertiary medical services across Nasarawa’s three senatorial zones, including the State Specialist Hospital, alongside the existing teaching hospital and Federal Medical Centre. On food security, the governor disclosed that 10,000 hectares had been committed to rice production. He also highlighted the state’s expanding mining sector, particularly lithium processing. He attributed the successes in the sector to supportive Federal Government policies aimed at encouraging greater value addition within producing states. items.title: Attack on Catholic Bishops is attack on entire Church, PFN fumes
items.description: •Vows to break bus preaching law By Olayinka Latona The National President of the Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria, PFN, Bishop Wale Oke, has thrown the full weight of the Pentecostal body behind the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria, declaring that any attack on the Catholic bishops is an attack on the entire Body of Christ. Speaking during an interview monitored by Sunday Vanguard, Bishop Oke endorsed the remarks made by John Onaiyekan during the recent visit of the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria, CBCN, to President Bola Tinubu, where the group told the President that “Nigeria is bleeding.” “Are we not bleeding? Are we not bleeding in Benue? Are we not bleeding in Southern Kaduna? Are we not bleeding in Gwoza, in Borno State? Are we not bleeding in Kwara? Are we not bleeding in Oyo State?” Oke queried, reiterating the Cardinal’s words verbatim. The PFN President challenged the government’s pushback against the bishops, insisting that speaking the truth to power is not a political act but a moral imperative. “Should anybody attack a Catholic bishop for saying that? That is the obvious truth,” he stated firmly. Bishop Oke dismissed attempts to isolate the Catholic bishops, emphasising Christian unity across denominations. “The Church of Jesus Christ is one. There may be many denominations, but we have one faith, one Lord, one baptism. The Church is one. If they attack the Catholic bishops, they are attacking the whole Church,” he declared. Plateau, Benue The PFN leader used the platform to condemn what he described as the government’s silence in the face of escalating violence against Christians, citing ongoing killings in Plateau, Southern Kaduna, Benue, Taraba, and recent incursions into Oyo, Kwara and Edo states by violent groups he linked to Islamic extremism. On the controversy surrounding the proposed amendment to the FRSC Act that would fine bus preachers ¦ 50,000, Bishop Oke was unequivocal. Despite the Senate’s clarification that the provision had existed since 2007 and was merely re-itemised, Oke insisted it must be expunged entirely. “We will break that law. Dear Senate of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, we will rather obey God than man,” he declared, adding that he has preached in buses since 1975 without causing any accident or distraction. “If you want to imprison us for preaching the gospel, we are ready. If you want to make all the stadiums in Nigeria prisons, we are ready. We would rather obey God than man,” he said defiantly. OIC withdrawal Beyond the bus preaching ban, Oke called on the National Assembly to address more fundamental issues, including Nigeria’s membership of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), which he said the country entered under military rule without the people’s consent. “The Senate should deal with that and pull Nigeria out of the OIC,” he demanded. He also renewed calls for a review of the 1999 Constitution, alleging it is skewed in favour of Islam. “In that Constitution, Islam is mentioned hundreds of times. Christianity is mentioned once. And Christians in Nigeria are a little over 50 per cent of the population,” he argued, insisting that the document was imposed by the “military jackboot” and does not represent the will of Nigerians. Genocide Bishop Oke doubled down on allegations of Christian genocide, accusing the government of spending billions to lobby against such claims in the United States while the killings continue. He distinguished between the primary targeting of Christians and the secondary killing of liberal Muslims who oppose extremist ideologies. “The Senate should invite the Church for a talk. Nigerians are being killed. You are sitting there making evil laws. We will break that law,” he concluded, reaffirming that the PFN is making private overtures to the Presidency even as it speaks publicly, though he declined to disclose details of those engagements. Timing Also, Pastor Seyi Osuntayo, Area Superintendent of The Apostolic Church Nigeria, Igbein Area, weighed in on the controversy, expressing concern about what he termed the “altercation” between the Presidency and the Catholic bishops. “The timing of the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria’s advice could be suspicious and be seen as partisan,” Pastor Osuntayo told our correspondent. “I feel the Catholic Bishops should have been talking about governance ab initio, not at the time of the electioneering campaign,” he noted. The cleric, who maintains that Christian leaders should not be involved in “political roforofo” but should focus on governance, cited the biblical instruction in 1 Timothy 2:1–4, urging Christians to pray for leaders regardless of their performance. “Our leaders need prayer, whether we agree with their views and leadership style or not. We may not get to choose our leader or their position on the issues we care about, but we can choose to be obedient to the Lord and cover them in prayer,” Osuntayo said. He cautioned against the increasing trend of Christian leaders creating media content or participating in news coverage to criticise the government, arguing that such actions only add to the political heat. “Instead of complaining or criticising, we can surrender our emotions and let the power of prayer take over. We never saw Jesus calling people to activism or rebellion against the Roman leaders who would ultimately kill Him,” he added. Political hypocrisy However, Ben Charles-Davies, a journalist and author, dismissed what he described as the government’s attempt to divert attention from the real issues. “My simple response to the verbal exchange between the Presidency and the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria is that it is unnecessary. The government is trying to divert attention from the main issue, which is poverty in the land,” Charles-Davies stated. He pointed to what he called “rank hypocrisy” in the government’s response, recalling that in November 2014, the CBCN, under the same Cardinal Onaiyekan, spoke against then-President Goodluck Jonathan’s administration’s handling of the economy. At the time, the opposition All Progressives Congress, APC, applauded and celebrated the cleric for being the voice of the voiceless. “Today, the APC government is angry because the same bishops informed them that Nigerians are going through socio-economic hardship and they are unhappy. That’s hypocrisy,” Charles-Davies asserted. He challenged government spokespersons to be more circumspect in attacking statesmen who hold contrary views, emphasising that “Nigeria belongs to all of us, not just those in government.” He further questioned the sincerity of government officials, asking: “Who in government, among ministers and advisers, can boldly tell the President the true situation of things in the country? Daily killings, kidnapping for ransom, food inflation, high transportation costs, collapsed health services, etc.? Not one. All of them are struggling to impress the President. Everything is going well. Nigerians are happy with the reforms.” He added that Cardinal Onaiyekan had simply expressed the feelings, pains and suffering of most Nigerians, regardless of their faith. Allegiance Ugoji Maximillian, a speaker, author and entrepreneur who was raised Catholic and attended a seminary, offered a more political analysis of the situation. “The Catholic bishops are a strong body. But they are highly political. They know how to play politics and can intimidate and threaten a politician using their structures,” Maximillian said. Maximillian, who claimed extensive knowledge of Catholic Church politics, gave a more controversial perspective, accusing the bishops of playing politics and attempting to intimidate the President. He traced the Church’s political influence across various states, citing examples of how Catholic clerics have shaped political outcomes in Enugu, Anambra, Imo, Benue and Kaduna states. “In 2023, they made a wrong move. That wrong move backfired. They put their eggs in one basket. They went all out for Peter Obi. They showed clearly that they disliked Tinubu. But they masked it by saying they were against the Muslim-Muslim ticket,” he added. The commentator argued that the bishops were “simply pursuing and supporting a candidate they felt was their boy, who would listen to them,” adding: “It pains influential men to be ignored by the one who rules their domains.” Economic progress On his part, a former Commissioner for Physical Planning in Lagos State, Mr Toyin Ayinde, offered a more nuanced perspective, suggesting that Nigerians have unrealistic expectations of change. “Politicians visiting a politician, and you want me to comment, especially when the former had openly shown, before the 2023 election, that they were pitched against the latter?” Ayinde questioned. He pointed to what he described as tangible economic progress, noting that his naira ATM card, which was previously unusable for online transactions, could now be used for purchases abroad. “I have, in the course of this year, made an online payment of about £4,500 using my naira ATM card, and while in Canada, I used my naira ATM card for most of my purchases. I didn’t need to use the dollar card.” Ayinde cautioned that “Nigerians don’t understand process, so everything must happen at microwave speed,” adding that the country is “heavily soaked in the culture of shaming.” “Rather than contribute advice for a guided way forward, we look for what to talk about in a disrespectful way to shame the other party,” he said. The post Attack on Catholic Bishops is attack on entire Church, PFN fumes appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: THE OUTRAGE MACHINE
items.description: A short video recently circulating on social media shows Adolf Hitler drinking from a can of Fanta while angrily proclaiming, “I hate juice.” Though millions mistook it for an authentic commercial, sparking fierce online debate, it is actually an AI-generated meme. Its artificial nature is fairly obvious, given that the colour, fonts and logo on the can look nothing like actual Fanta packaging. So why did so many people fall for it? The answer lies in our current media topography, where “shockvertising” has been methodically normalised. The term ‘shockvertising’ emerged in the early 1990s, though the practice dates back to public health campaigns in the late 1960s, and describes a marketing strategy that deliberately violates social, moral or aesthetic boundaries to startle, offend or disturb an audience. Unlike traditional advertisements that highlight product benefits, shockvertising relies on instinctive reactions like fear, disgust, horror or outrage to cut through commercial noise. This is done to drive high brand recall and generate free publicity. Due to the fact that real brands have pushed boundaries in the recent past, a concept as absurd as a Hitler-themed Fanta advertisement suddenly felt plausible to an over-stimulated public. In an online world where algorithms reward anger over accuracy, outrage has become one of the most valuable forms of currency in the digital age The earliest examples of shockvertising emerged in the late 1960s and early 1970s through Western government funded anti-smoking campaigns, which featured graphic images of diseased lungs. While these visuals shocked audiences, the public largely accepted them because they served the purpose of raising awareness about smoking-related illnesses. Eventually, governments made it a legal requirement for tobacco companies to print these graphic images directly on cigarette packets. Seeing how receptive people were to shocking imagery when tied to a meaningful cause, and recognising its power to ignite widespread public debate, several consumer brands decided to adopt similar tactics to shatter the clutter of traditional advertising. In the late 1980s, Italian clothing brand United Colours of Benetton transformed shockvertising into a corporate strategy. Instead of displaying clothes, Benetton ran controversial photographs of a dying AIDS activist, a priest kissing a nun and blood-soaked war uniforms, linking the brand directly to concentrated social debates. Luxury brands such as Gucci and Tom Ford later introduced hyper-sexualised, taboo imagery to build an ‘edgy’, exclusive identity, often actively courting media bans to secure free publicity. Illustration by Abro Modern shock tactics have since migrated online, leaning heavily into ‘rage-baiting’ and controversial social stances engineered specifically to drive viral outrage, heated debate and clicks across digital platforms. Shockvertising is an offshoot of what is often referred to as the “outrage economy.” American media theorists Tim Wu and Shoshana Zuboff describe the outrage economy as a digital marketplace where human attention is monetised through heightened conflict and anger. Rather than promoting a brand on its merits or presenting a topic through objective analysis, the outrage economy banks on manufactured outrage to bypass critical thinking, instantly capturing attention and high digital traffic through viral sharing and continuous debate. Social media ‘influencers’ and vloggers frequently resort to making absurd claims and spreading outright falsehoods, purely to inflate their views and comment sections. Far from discouraging this behaviour, social media platforms reward it. Their underlying algorithms are engineered to prioritise high engagement above truth, effectively monetising outrageous content and turning controversy into a business model. Pakistani comedian Tabish Hashmi recently sparked widespread online debate by announcing his departure from a Geo TV show that he hosts. Disappointed fans quickly flooded social media platforms, but their dismay rapidly morphed into outrage after a rumour surfaced claiming Hashmi had been fired over controversial remarks regarding political unrest in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). Remarkably, those expressing outrage rarely paused to verify the nature, or even the existence, of the supposed comments. In reality, no such statements were ever made. The entire episode was a staged publicity stunt. Hashmi was never asked to leave and Geo TV had merely paused production briefly to redesign the show’s set. For days, however, the host and the programme dominated digital discourse. The manufactured controversy allowed observers to project their own political narratives on to the event, with some reading complex state conspiracies into the hiatus and others extending outrage over perceived censorship. The situation raises certain questions about this strategy. Did Geo need to engineer a hoax to boost lagging ratings? But more amusing was the swiftness with which Geo and Hashmi ultimately dismissed the incident as a harmless “prank”. This may suggest a sudden loss of nerve once the audience transformed a routine promotional stunt into a tense conversation about free speech and anti-establishment rhetoric. After the hoax was revealed, many felt disappointed, and even embarrassed, at having been so easily duped. Yet, this vulnerability to manipulation is no longer an anomaly. In an era dominated by swift digital communication and heightened emotional engagement, such impressionability has ceased to be an exception. It has become the standard condition of the modern audience. The media in general and brands are aware of this. It has become easy for manufactured outrage to profit from growing gullibility. When digital platforms actively reward sensationalism over accuracy, critical thinking takes a back seat to knee-jerk reactions. As a result, audiences have grown increasingly susceptible to manufactured narratives, routinely accepting outrage at face value before taking the time to verify basic facts. Politicians, corporate brands, influencers, vloggers, mainstream media outlets and even everyday users all feed this cycle. It is no wonder, then, that the concept of online “trending topics” has so seamlessly replaced genuine public discourse, turning meaningful dialogue into an algorithmic spectacle. To paraphrase the American media theorist Neil Postman, the spectacle is designed for consumption rather than comprehension. Published in Dawn, EOS, August 9th, 2026

items.title: Six months in captivity: Woro freed victims recount ordeal
items.description: •Young women married off •Some male captives joined terrorists’ camp •OFFICIAL: Survivors tested positive to acute malaria fever, malnutrition By Demola Akinyemi Six months after they were abducted by terrorists, survivors of the Woro community attack in Kaiama Local Government Area of Kwara State have recounted the harrowing experiences they endured in captivity, including the deaths of 13 children, forced marriages involving some young women and severe hunger and deprivation. The victims were abducted on February 3, 2026, when terrorists attacked the community. The survivors, who were rescued by security forces and officially handed over to the Kwara State Government on Friday, narrated their ordeal while meeting with Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq in Ilorin. Meanwhile, medical examinations conducted on the released victims have revealed that some of them tested positive for acute malaria and malnutrition. Sunday Vanguard gathered that selected officials of the Kwara State Ministry of Health commenced intensive medical examinations on the remaining released victims at a designated hotel in the Government Reserved Area, GRA, Ilorin, where they are being accommodated. Fourteen of the victims, whose conditions were said to be critical when they arrived in Ilorin on Thursday night, have been transferred to the Kwara State University Teaching Hospital, Ilorin, for further medical attention. A source in the Ministry of Health, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the tests conducted so far showed that some of the victims were suffering from acute malaria and malnutrition. Asked about the possible causes of the conditions, the official said: “We only treated them based on the results we obtained after carrying out the tests. Ours is not to ask them questions about the environment they lived in or how they were treated.” Recounting her experience, one of the survivors, Ameerah Saliu, said she assisted in delivering 11 pregnant women while in captivity, but only about half of the babies survived. Ameerah, who identified herself as a health worker, said she had to rely on her professional knowledge to assist the pregnant women despite the harsh conditions in the terrorists’ camp. “It was like living in hell and striving to stay alive. At one point, all hope was lost, but thanks to Almighty Allah, freedom eventually came. “I’m a health worker, so I just had to assist the women to deliver. I delivered, I think, about 11 babies, but only half of them survived due to the terrible and harsh environment,” she said. She disclosed that 13 children died in the camp as a result of the harsh conditions, while some young women were married off and some young men eventually joined the terrorists’ camp. “Ultimately, 13 children died due to the very bad conditions, and the experience was quite harrowing, seeing their death and burial,” she said. According to her, the women were not sexually molested during their captivity, but they were subjected to severe hunger and deprivation. “We were fed with anything, like kulikuli, and given any water, maybe once in a day, just to keep whoever could stay alive,” she said. Ameerah said the victims had almost lost hope of regaining their freedom before their eventual rescue. She expressed appreciation to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Kwara State Government and the security agencies for securing their freedom. Another survivor, Hauwa Saliu, one of the wives of the Woro village head, corroborated Ameerah’s account, describing their experience in captivity as one that was difficult to put into words. “None of us believed we would ever be freed again, and so we resigned to fate. Interestingly, they pray too, but Almighty Allah is merciful. Those experiences can’t be recounted. But we are happy for freedom today,” she said. Receiving the victims, Governor AbdulRazaq commended President Tinubu and the security agencies for the successful rescue operation. He described the operation as a demonstration of the Federal Government’s commitment to protecting lives and restoring peace to communities affected by terrorism and banditry. The governor assured the survivors of the state government’s continued support, rehabilitation and reintegration. He said government would continue to provide the necessary assistance to help the victims recover from the trauma and challenges associated with their prolonged captivity. Sunday Vanguard gathered that 46 of the rescued survivors are currently receiving medical treatment at the Kwara State University Teaching Hospital The post Six months in captivity: Woro freed victims recount ordeal appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Infantino denies allegations of affair, favouritism while at UEFA
items.description: PARIS: FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who has endured a week of scathing criticism revolving around the now shelved private investment plan, has been accused by a British newspaper of paying off an alleged lover while at UEFA. According to The Telegraph , the Italian-Swiss lawyer, who served as secretary general of European football’s governing body from 2009 to 2016, also previously used his influence to secure a promotion for the same UEFA employee with whom he was in an intimate relationship. Infantino has categorically denied the allegations, according to the article which was published late on Friday. When contacted by AFP on Saturday, a FIFA spokesperson had not responded. According to The Telegraph , which did not cite its sources, this employee received a “a six-figure sum” upon her departure — at an unspecified time — in addition to the payment of tuition fees for a business school amounting to around 45,000 ($60,700). When contacted by AFP , UEFA acknowledged that “a departure payment was made to the individual in question” at that time, “coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school”. However, it insisted “the payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time”, before adding that “such regulations have been tightened since 2016”. Quoted by The Telegraph , a FIFA spokesperson stated that Infantino, who has been married since 2001, “strongly denies these allegations”, which were “categorically untrue”. “Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory,” FIFA added. “No employee at UEFA and FIFA has ever raised a complaint regarding Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved.” Infantino, who is standing for re-election next March, has been embroiled in a crisis since the announcement late last month of his controversial — and ultimately abandoned — plan to open up the World Cup to private investors. He faces opposition in particular from UEFA, which on Thursday stood by its threat to boycott the World Cups, deeming the mere withdrawal of the controversial plan to be insufficient. Published in Dawn, August 9th, 2026

items.title: Nigeria may lose out on fresh $1.4bn US health aid over Christians persecution
items.description: By Nkiruka Nnorom Nigeria may be excluded from a new $1.4 billion U.S health and humanitarian assistance package announced earlier this week if the Federal Government fails to take measurable actions to address violence against Christians, according to terms contained in a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding signed by both countries. The MOU, signed on December 20, 2025 between the U.S Department of State and the Nigerian government under the America First Global Health Strategy, AFGHS, commits Washington to nearly $2.1 billion over five years to expand preventative and curative services for HIV, TB, malaria, maternal and child health and polio. Under the MoU, Nigeria is also expected to increase its domestic health spending by nearly $3 billion during the term, an expenditure that has been described as the largest co-investment under AFGHS. A significant portion of the U.S funding is earmarked for Nigeria’s 900 faith-based clinics and hospitals, which currently serve more than 30 percent of Nigerians.However, the deal contains strict conditions. The MOU states that the agreement was “negotiated in connection with reforms the Nigerian government has made to prioritize protecting Christian populations from violence” and includes “significant dedicated funding” for Christian health facilities. Crucially, it adds: “As with all foreign assistance, the President and Secretary of State retain the right to pause or terminate any programme which do not align with the national interest, and the Trump administration expects Nigeria to continue to make progress ensuring that it combats extremist religious violence against vulnerable Christian populations.” The conditionality was reinforced by the U.S House of Representatives, which recently voted to tie Nigeria’s aid to verifiable steps on tackling Christian persecution. The bill passed last month by the House of Rep tasked Abuja with taking concrete actions to ensure the return of internally displaced persons to their ancestral homes and ensuring protection for persecuted Christians in the Middle Belt region among others. Meanwhile, in the fresh aid approved by Washington under its AFGHS, the U.S set aside $1.4 billion to support integrated health services through faith and community-based hospitals and clinics in more than 20 countries. Out of it, $850 million will go through a Faith and Community Initiative Award to World Vision and local faith-based implementers to strengthen over 2,500 faith-based hospitals and clinics across 17 countries with more than 30,000 community health workers trained, paid, and equipped. An additional $570 million will be channeled directly to faith-based and community hospitals through bilateral MOUs with governments, including Nigeria. In humanitarian assistance, the State Department also announced $538 million for Samaritan’s Purse and a World Vision–Compassion International consortium to reach 7 million people across 16 humanitarian crises. Over $100 million will be made immediately available for disaster response in 23 disaster-prone countries. The State Department said the combined $1.4 billion health announcement is the largest to faith-based organizations in over 20 years, with at least 80 percent of resources required to go directly to frontline services. For Nigeria, the MOU specifically emphasized support for Christian faith-based health care providers, which are described in the agreement as “uniquely positioned” to complement public facilities. With the U.S shifting more resources to faith-based delivery where such providers account for 40 per cent or more of health facilities in many aid-recipient countries, Nigeria’s access to the new funding will depend on how Abuja addresses concerns raised in Washington. The State Department said partners like Samaritan’s Purse, World Vision and Compassion International were chosen for their record of rapid deployment in conflict zones and disaster areas without bureaucratic delay. The post Nigeria may lose out on fresh $1.4bn US health aid over Christians persecution appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: OSUN VIOLENCE: We’re the victims, Adeleke is playing victim to curry sympathy – Oyebamiji
items.description: By Adetutu Oyebanjo Governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Osun State, Biodun Oyebamiji, has accused Governor Ademola Adeleke of playing the victim to curry sympathy ahead of Saturday’s governorship poll. Adeleke has repeatedly accused the APC of attacking his administration and members of his party, Accord Party, to instill fear ahead of the election. Meanwhile, Oyebamiji denied the accusation, saying he and other members of the APC were the true victims of political violence in the state. Addressing newsmen, the former Chief Executive Officer of the National Inland Waterways Authority, NIWA, also accused the ruling party of killing several members of the state’s APC from 2023 to date. His words: “We are the victims. The governor is just playing the victim to curry sympathy. In his mind, he knows the truth. Therefore, let me seize this opportunity to reassure Osun people and Nigerians, through you, that both the APC and I are the real victims of persistent political violence in Osun State. “During the 2022 governorship election, more than 25 members of our party were murdered by members of the political party in power in Osun. In my own local government area for example, the Chairman of Irewole Local Government Area, Remi Abass, was killed within the council secretariat last year. “From 2023 to date, several of our members and other Osun citizens have been killed by agents of government. Our party has also documented several other politically motivated attacks and killings, for which we continue to seek justice through the courts. Therefore, the ongoing political violence has all the signs of government in power on it. Just recently, the Inspector-General of Police visited Osun State and publicly raised allegations concerning individuals accused of criminal activities being housed within the Government House. Recent reports indicate that some of our members were attacked in Ede, the hometown of Governor Adeleke. As an opposition party, these are some of the experiences of members of our party. Ironically, it is the Accord Party and government of Adeleke that are crying foul while our members bear the scars of political violence.” On his plans if elected, he said: “Once the good people of Osun hand me the mandate, we will, in line with our campaign promises, within our first 100 days in office, undertake a comprehensive review of all outstanding entitlements owed to active and retired workers and commence immediate payment. We are equally committed to to ensuring that the Dagbolu Dry Port becomes fully operational. In addition to these, through strategic partnerships, we will commence the training and empowerment of no fewer than 10,000 young people in information and communication technology. We will also institutionalise monthly monthly meetings of the State Security Council involving security agencies, traditional rulers and local government leaders.” The post OSUN VIOLENCE: We’re the victims, Adeleke is playing victim to curry sympathy – Oyebamiji appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Karachi's Red Line suffers another blow as decision to cancel Mosamiyat-to-Numaish contract declared ‘invalid’
items.description: KARACHI: In a major blow to hopes of easing Karachi’s transportation crisis anytime soon, the Sindh government’s decision to cancel the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Red Line construction contract has been declared “unlawful, invalid, null and void”. The ruling was delivered by the Dispute Resolution Board after the Sindh High Court asked the parties to approach the forum. The Dispute Board’s decision also delivered an extraordinary indictment of the very agency entrusted with executing the project — TransKarachi — questioning its institutional capacity and pointing out its lack of experienced project management needed to administer a project of this magnitude and complexity. The contract requires both the employer (TransKarachi/Sindh government) and the contractor to resolve the dispute through an independent Dispute Board before resorting to formal court lawsuits. The Sindh government had announced termination of the BRT Red Line project’s key segment called Lot-2 from Mosamiyat to Numaish, over “lack of progress”. Immediately, the construction company, AM Associate, filed a constitutional petition in the Sindh High Court challenging the government’s decision and accused the provincial government of delaying the scheme. Decision, in favour of contractor, by Dispute Resolution Board declares TransKarachi, the Sindh govt-owned implementation agency, lacked institutional capacity to manage the project The High Court directed both parties to abide by their signed agreement and ordered the activation of the Dispute Board as pre-agreed contract terms. After more than two months of hearings, the Dispute Board has declared the government’s cancellation of the contract unlawful and invalid. It said that decision was taken in haste, without considering the complexity of the project. The board also declared that the government-owned company TransKarachi’s lacked institutional capacity to manage a project of this scale. “The evidence indicates that the Employer [TransKarachi] lacked the institutional capacity and sufficiently experienced project management necessary to administer a project of this magnitude and complexity,” said the board’s in its detailed decision, a copy of which is available with Dawn . The board’s verdict has now exposed a far more explosive reality that the problem is not simply with the contractor’s performance, but the project’s own implementing agency, Sindh government-owned TransKarachi, lacked the capacity to deliver the project. It found that the TransKarachi had been unable to fulfil “several of its fundamental contractual obligations” at the commencement of the works. The design had not been finalised, possession of the entire site free from encumbrances had not been provided, numerous physical obstructions remained and substantial payments due to the contractor were outstanding, it said. According to the board, these matters “materially affected the Contractor’s ability to execute the works” and “substantially contributed to the delays encountered during the performance of the contract”. The Dispute Board has pointed failures in fulfilling basic contractual obligations, deficiencies in project administration, repeated design revisions, inadequate coordination, delayed decision-making and a lack of evidence that available alternatives to termination were properly considered. The shortcomings, it added, were compounded by deficiencies in the performance and coordination of the engineer and consultants, resulting in “ineffective contract administration and delayed decision-making throughout the Project”. On the decision to terminate, the board said the Engineer and Consultants should have advised the Employer to pursue reasonable contractual alternatives, given the scale and complexity of the project and the practical constraints surrounding its execution. “The board has seen no evidence that these, or any other less drastic measures, were meaningfully considered,” it added. Instead, the board found that insufficient attention had been given to resolving outstanding issues. “In the board’s view, effective and proactive contract management could reasonably have preserved the contract,” it said. The board concluded that the evidence did not demonstrate that the decision to terminate the contract had been preceded by a genuine consideration of the contractual alternatives available. The termination, it therefore found, “was premature and was not a measure of last resort”. Published in Dawn, August 9th, 2026

items.title: Court sentences barber for dumping refuse in public drain
items.description: A Hohoe Magistrate Court has sentenced Ekpane Seyram, a barber for collecting and dumping rubbish into a public drain. Ekpane pleaded guilty to the charge and was sentenced on his own plea to a fine of GHS 600 or would serve two months in prison in default. Mr Daniel Dotse Eklo, Environmental Health Analyst, Prosecuting, told the court, presided over by the relieving judge, Mr Lambert Y. Keriba, that the convict on Monday July 27, at about 2000 hours was caught dumping rubbish into the public drain around the Konuvie Plaza area. He said the activity of the convict was captured on a video and subsequently shared on Facebook. Mr Eklo said the incident caught the attention of the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) and the Environmental Health Office at about 2126 hours the same day. He said the Environmental Health Unit in collaboration with the MCE through an investigation got the convict on Wednesday at about 1030 hours who accepted liability to the offence upon interrogation. Mr Eklo said the convict added that he collected the rubbish in and around a drinking bar where he had been staying belonging to one Madam Cecilia Attamah and Vincentia Attamah around the Konuvie area and dumped the same in the public drain around the area. He said the Assembly placed skip containers at vantage points in the Municipality for the collection and proper disposal of refuse. He said: “The Konuvie area is behind the Total Fuel Station around the station traffic light which is just about 150 meters from the Low Cost down and Market area container site.” He described the convict’s action as barbaric and inimical to the environment which could lead to flooding and outbreak of diseases.
